i.241469105:
LPH performed an electrical system check and investigated multiple receptacles that were not working throughout the kitchen, dining room, and living room. During today’s evaluation, we identified several electrical concerns involving failed receptacle connections, exposed attic wiring, improper breaker configurations at the main panel, and an outdated subpanel with grounding and neutral deficiencies. We also identified opportunities to improve GFCI protection and exterior lighting around the garage.

The following summarizes our findings, recommendations, and the options discussed with the homeowner.

Living Room – Failed Receptacles and Electrical Connections

LPH investigated the loss of power affecting receptacles in the living room and found that several older stab-back connections had failed, resulting in electrical arcing and dead spots along the circuit. These connections rely on spring tension to maintain contact with the wiring, and as they deteriorate over time, they can create unreliable electrical connections, excessive heat, and potential arcing.

LPH recommends replacing the three affected receptacles and repairing the associated wiring splices to restore reliable electrical operation. Due to the age of the existing devices and the failures already occurring, we also discussed a whole-home device restoration option to proactively replace the switches and receptacles throughout the home.

Kitchen and Dining Room – Loss of Power and Attic Wiring Concerns

The kitchen and dining room wall receptacles were found to have no power. LPH traced the affected circuit into the attic, where we discovered multiple energized wires and electrical splices that were not enclosed in approved junction boxes. These exposed connections were lying on the ceiling, leaving the wiring vulnerable to accidental contact and other damage.

During troubleshooting, we also discovered that the wiring originally supplying the affected receptacles had been tapped into and repurposed to supply lighting, resulting in the loss of power to the receptacle circuit.

LPH identified a way to restore power to the affected receptacles. The recommended attic wiring repair includes safely enclosing the exposed wiring splices in approved junction boxes, restoring power to the kitchen and dining room receptacle circuit using additional wiring in the attic, and installing an additional junction box as needed to protect the new connections.

Correcting these conditions will help restore reliable power and reduce the risks associated with exposed electrical splices and improperly protected wiring connections.

Main Electrical Panel – Breaker Sizing and Wiring Terminations

During the inspection of the main electrical panel, LPH identified two 20-amp breakers supplying wiring that includes 14-gauge conductors. These breakers appear to be oversized for the wiring and may not provide the proper level of overcurrent protection.

LPH recommends correcting this configuration by installing a properly sized 2-pole 15-amp breaker, provided the circuit arrangement and wiring are suitable for this configuration.

We also found two additional breakers with multiple wires connected under a single terminal. Unless the breakers are specifically listed for multiple conductors at those terminals, these connections may create unreliable electrical contact, overheating, and potential arcing.

LPH recommends correcting these connections by properly separating and pigtailing the conductors where appropriate or installing additional breakers to accommodate the wiring, depending on the panel’s capacity and the applicable equipment requirements.

Existing Subpanel – Outdated ITE Pushmatic Equipment

LPH also identified an older ITE Pushmatic subpanel that appears to date back to approximately the 1960s. Due to the age and type of equipment, its long-term reliability and serviceability are concerns. Some insurance companies may also restrict coverage for homes containing this type of equipment, depending on the carrier and the panel’s condition.

Additional concerns were found within the subpanel. The circuit grounding conductors were not properly arranged on a separate grounding bar, and most of the neutral conductors serving the outgoing circuits had been cut short or cut off. We also identified a basement receptacle that was not working due to what appears to be an open neutral, with the subpanel being a suspected source.

LPH recommends replacing the existing subpanel and correcting the associated grounding, neutral, and wiring deficiencies to meet applicable electrical requirements. This would provide an opportunity to address the existing installation concerns, investigate the suspected open neutral, and improve the long-term reliability and serviceability of the home’s electrical distribution system.

Bathroom – Failed GFCI Receptacle

During the system check, LPH found a bathroom GFCI receptacle that was no longer functioning properly. GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of electrical shock by interrupting power when a ground-fault condition is detected.

LPH recommends replacing the failed GFCI receptacle to restore this important safety feature.

Basement Laundry Area – Additional GFCI Protection

The washing machine receptacle in the basement is located near the wash sink and does not currently have GFCI protection. Given the proximity to water, LPH recommends installing a GFCI receptacle to provide additional protection against electrical shock.

Whole-Home Device Restoration – Additional Option Discussed

Due to the age of the home’s switches and receptacles and the failures already identified with the existing stab-back connections, LPH discussed the option of replacing all switches and receptacles throughout the home.

This proactive upgrade would eliminate the existing stab-back connection points at the devices being replaced and establish new electrical connections throughout the home. It would also reduce the likelihood of future device-related failures and provide greater peace of mind for the coming decades.

As part of the proposed package, LPH offered to include the attic wiring repairs and both GFCI upgrades at no additional charge. This option provides a more comprehensive approach to addressing the existing device and circuit concerns rather than waiting for additional failures to occur.

Garage – Two Motion-Sensor Floodlights

LPH recommended installing two motion-sensor floodlights around the garage to improve exterior visibility and provide automatic lighting when movement is detected. These lights will help illuminate the surrounding areas after dark, improve visibility when entering or exiting the garage, and provide additional convenience and awareness of activity around the property.

Discussion With Homeowner and Approved Work

LPH contacted Robin by phone and reviewed the available options, explaining the electrical concerns identified during the evaluation and the recommended repairs and upgrades.

After discussing the options, Robin elected to move forward with the repairs addressing the identified issues at the main electrical panel, the living room receptacles, and the kitchen and dining room receptacle circuits. The approved work includes correcting the identified breaker issues at the main panel, replacing the affected living room receptacles and repairing the associated connections, restoring power to the kitchen and dining room receptacle circuit, completing the attic wiring repairs, and installing both GFCI receptacles.

The installation of two motion-sensor floodlights around the garage is also included in the approved work.

The approved work is scheduled for November 5th, and a down payment has been collected.

The replacement of the existing ITE Pushmatic subpanel and the whole-home device restoration were also discussed as additional options but are not included in the currently approved scope of work.

Today’s electrical evaluation and all associated estimates will be emailed to Robin for her records and future reference.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate the opportunity to help improve the safety, reliability, and functionality of your electrical system and look forward to completing the scheduled work.

Stab-back connections rely on spring tension to maintain electrical contact with the wiring. * Included at no additional charge: Replace the failed bathroom GFCI receptacle.
* Included at no additional charge: Install GFCI protection at the basement washing machine receptacle near the wash sink.

Why We Recommend This Upgrade

With multiple older stab-back connections already experiencing failures, replacing the devices throughout the home provides a proactive solution instead of continuing to address problems one receptacle or switch at a time. This allows LPH to eliminate the existing stab-back connection points being replaced and establish fresh electrical connections throughout the home.

i.304196138:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, two electrical concerns were brought to our attention prior to our electrical inspection. The first concern was, their low-voltage spotlights on the deck post that were not working. We were able to confirm that none of these fixtures were getting proper power, and we provided an option to rerun this circuit from the transformer. The second concern was the dining table light would randomly turn on sometimes in the evening/night. We identified that the existing switches are the adorne smart switches. We also identified that the wiring for the switch was not connected properly and we corrected this issue today. The homeowners will inform us if this issue continues. 


We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

i.313600655:
Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. During my evaluation, I found that most of the baseboard outlets are ungrounded. Ungrounded receptacles are a safety concern, particularly when three-prong appliances or equipment are plugged into them. In the event of an electrical fault, an improperly grounded system can create a potential shock hazard by allowing energized metal components to become electrically charged.

I also observed that the main electrical panel is advanced in age. Due to the age of the equipment, replacement is recommended. Electrical panels and their internal safety components can deteriorate over time, and older circuit breakers may become less reliable and may fail to trip properly during an overload or fault condition. This can increase the risk of overheating and electrical damage.

Additionally, the building’s water piping system is not properly bonded/grounded. A properly sized grounding/bonding conductor should be installed from the main electrical service to the water piping system near the water meter. This provides a proper path for fault current and helps reduce the risk of electrical shock when using metal plumbing fixtures.

The customer advised that they will address the ungrounded receptacles. However, they requested an estimate for replacement of the main electrical panel and installation of the required water-piping grounding/bonding connection.

All available solutions were presented to the customer. An estimate for the requested work was provided separately.

i.316326921:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, Sabina reported two concerns/questions that she had for her electrical system. The first was her LED puck lights in her bedroom would flicker briefly every time she adjusted her ceiling fan speed. We informed Sabina that her LED lights are reading the harmonic interference, which is causing these lights to respond to that interference. Installing an electronic based control system instead of a mechanical will help alleviate the harmonic interference that she’s witnessing with these fixtures. She also informed us of a LED puck light that would struggle turn on sometimes and also flicker periodically when on. We informed Sabina that this fixture’s internal driver is failing and the entire fixture will need to be swapped out to remedy this. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does not meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was identifying all the existing smoke detectors are past their 10 year lifespan. Lastly, we identified an area with missing GFI protection, which is in the kitchen. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

LPH performed an electrical system evaluation and identified significant concerns with the home’s existing electrical service. The approximately 35-year-old Siemens electrical panel is experiencing active arcing at the main breaker, accompanied by audible buzzing consistent with internal arcing and flickering lights throughout the home. These symptoms indicate a serious electrical hazard that requires immediate attention.

In addition to the concerns inside the home, LPH found deterioration affecting the exterior electrical service. The underground conduit has cracked and separated from the meter base, creating a potential entry point for water into the electrical service equipment. The existing meter base sealing has also cracked and deteriorated, compromising its ability to prevent moisture intrusion.

The insulation on the incoming service cable has developed yellow discoloration consistent with deterioration and possible contamination associated with aluminum oxide, a byproduct of corrosion on aluminum conductors. Corrosion at electrical service connections can compromise conductivity, increase electrical resistance, contribute to overheating, and lead to unreliable electrical operation.

Due to the combination of active arcing, flickering lights, compromised exterior service components, potential water intrusion, and signs of deterioration affecting the incoming service cable, LPH strongly recommends a complete 200 Amp electrical service upgrade rather than replacing the interior panel alone. This comprehensive approach addresses the concerns affecting both the interior electrical panel and the exterior service equipment.

Approved Option: Complete 200 Amp Electrical Service Upgrade

LPH reviewed the findings with the homeowner in detail and recommended a complete modernization of the home’s electrical service to address the existing safety concerns and improve long-term reliability.

The approved scope of work includes:

* Complete Exterior Electrical Service Replacement: Replace the existing meter base with a new 200 Amp meter base, install new service entrance conductors and a new service head as required, repair the damaged underground conduit connection, and properly seal the meter base and associated entry points to help prevent moisture intrusion. Protective conduit will be installed over the exterior service cable where applicable to help protect against sunlight exposure, physical damage, and premature insulation deterioration.
* New 200 Amp Exterior Emergency Disconnect: Install a new exterior emergency service disconnect with the required connections, identification, and labeling. This provides an accessible means of shutting off power to the home during an emergency or when electrical service work is necessary, improving accessibility for emergency responders and electrical service personnel.
* Interior Electrical Panel Replacement: Remove the existing approximately 35-year-old Siemens panel and install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel. Existing branch circuits will be transferred and properly terminated with appropriately sized breakers. Accessible conductors and connections will be inspected for signs of heat damage, corrosion, or deterioration, and the new panel will be properly labeled.
* Whole-Home Surge Protection: Install a whole-home surge protective device at the new electrical panel to help protect sensitive electronics, appliances, and other connected equipment against damaging voltage surges caused by lightning, utility disturbances, and other electrical events.
* Complete Grounding and Bonding Upgrade: Upgrade the grounding electrode system as required, including two grounding electrodes where required, properly sized grounding electrode conductors, and verification of the bonding of applicable metal water piping and other qualifying metal systems. This work helps establish a properly configured grounding and bonding system so electrical protective devices can operate as intended during a fault.
* Permits, Inspections, and Utility Coordination: LPH will coordinate with PPL as required, obtain the necessary permits, arrange required inspections, and complete the installation in accordance with applicable electrical codes and utility requirements. The completed installation will be tested to verify proper operation.

This comprehensive upgrade will replace the compromised electrical service components, address the identified concerns, and provide modern electrical distribution equipment with additional capacity for the home’s existing and future electrical needs.

Bathroom Exhaust Fan Replacement – Three Fans

During the evaluation, LPH also identified that the home’s three existing exhaust fans are nearing the end of their service life, with some of the fan motors no longer operating.

A properly functioning exhaust fan is important for removing excess moisture from bathrooms. When fans stop working or no longer provide adequate ventilation, moisture can accumulate and contribute to condensation and potential moisture-related damage over time.

LPH recommended replacing all three existing fans with Panasonic Whisper Quiet exhaust fans, designed for quiet operation, reliable performance, and a service life of 20+ years under normal operating conditions.

Replacing all three fans together will help restore dependable bathroom ventilation, reduce excess moisture buildup, and minimize the inconvenience of additional fan failures as the remaining aging fans continue to deteriorate.

e.346674595:
Emergency Electrical Panel Replacement – Critical Safety Concern

LPH found the home’s existing 35-year-old Siemens electrical panel experiencing active electrical arcing at the main breaker. The main breaker was producing audible buzzing consistent with internal arcing, and the homeowner reported flickering lights throughout the home. These symptoms indicate a serious electrical concern that requires immediate attention.

Electrical arcing occurs when electrical current jumps across an unintended gap or compromised connection. This can generate excessive heat, damage electrical components, and increase the risk of electrical fires. The accompanying flickering lights may indicate an unstable electrical connection, making it important to address the condition rather than continue operating the affected equipment.

Due to the active arcing at the main breaker, the age of the existing panel, and the symptoms occurring throughout the home, LPH recommends an emergency replacement of the existing electrical panel to address this immediate safety concern and restore reliable electrical distribution.

Scope of Work Includes:

* Remove the existing 35-year-old Siemens electrical panel.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel.
* Transfer and properly terminate the existing branch circuit wiring, inspecting accessible conductors and connections during installation.
* Install appropriately sized breakers for the existing circuits.
* Inspect and verify electrical connections and terminations.
* Properly label the new electrical panel and identify the circuits.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation of the electrical system.

Why This Replacement Is Important

Replacing the existing panel will eliminate the deteriorated panel and main breaker assembly as a source of the observed arcing, provided the fault is isolated to the equipment being replaced. The new panel will provide modern electrical distribution equipment, improved reliability, and additional breaker space for the home’s electrical needs.

Because the reported symptoms can also be associated with problems elsewhere in the electrical service, the incoming service conductors, meter base, and associated connections should be evaluated as part of the repair. Replacing the panel alone will not correct deterioration or water intrusion originating in the exterior service equipment.

LPH strongly recommends addressing this condition immediately. Active arcing at the main breaker is not a condition that should be left operating while waiting for a future upgrade. If the equipment is continuing to arc, it should be kept de-energized by a qualified professional until it can be safely repaired or replaced.

A water softener is a home water treatment system that removes the minerals responsible for hard water, primarily calcium and magnesium. These minerals are naturally found in groundwater and can build up in your plumbing, appliances, and fixtures over time.
A water softener helps make water gentler on your plumbing, improves soap performance, and reduces mineral buildup throughout your home.
How does a water softener work?
Most traditional water softeners use a process called ion exchange.
Water enters the system. Hard water flows through a tank containing special resin beads.
Minerals are removed. The resin captures calcium and magnesium and exchanges them for sodium or, in some systems, potassium.
Softened water flows through your home. The treated water goes to your showers, sinks, washing machine, dishwasher, and other connected fixtures.
The system regenerates. Periodically, it uses a salt solution to clean the resin and flush the collected minerals away.
Despite the name, a water softener doesn't necessarily remove dirt, bacteria, chlorine, or other contaminants. Those require different treatment methods.
The 7 biggest benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale and mineral buildup
Helps prevent the white, chalky deposits that accumulate on faucets, showerheads, glass, and plumbing fixtures. It can also reduce scale buildup inside water-using appliances.
2. Better showering and bathing
Many people find soap and shampoo rinse off more easily with soft water. It can leave skin feeling less coated with mineral residue and hair feeling smoother, although individual results vary.
3. Less soap and detergent needed
Soft water allows soap and many detergents to lather and clean more effectively. You may be able to use less laundry detergent, dishwashing detergent, and certain household cleaning products.
4. Helps protect appliances
Reducing scale can help water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other appliances operate more efficiently and may extend their useful life, especially where the water is very hard.
5. Fewer spots on dishes and glassware
Softened water can reduce mineral spots and cloudy residue on glassware, shower doors, and dishes. Dishwasher results also depend on detergent and rinse-aid settings.
6. Reduced plumbing scale
A properly sized and maintained system helps prevent hard mineral deposits from accumulating inside pipes, valves, and water fixtures.
7. Easier household cleaning
With less mineral residue, you may spend less time scrubbing shower doors, sinks, and faucets. Soap scum can also be easier to manage.
e.345546198:
A Moen Flo is a smart water-monitoring and leak-protection system that installs on your home's main water supply line. Its primary purpose is to help detect leaks, monitor water usage, and automatically shut off the water to your home if it identifies a potentially serious problem.
Unlike a water softener, which treats hard water, a Moen Flo helps protect your home from water damage.
How does Moen Flo work?
The system monitors water flowing through your home's plumbing and learns typical water-use patterns. It can identify unusual activity, such as continuous water flow or a small leak, and notify you through its connected app.
Depending on the detected condition and your settings, it can automatically shut off the main water supply to help prevent damage.
The 6 main benefits of Moen Flo
1. Helps prevent costly water damage
If a pipe bursts or a major leak occurs, Flo can automatically shut off your home's water supply. This is particularly valuable when you're away on vacation or at work. ￼
2. Detects small, hidden leaks
Its daily leak tests can identify leaks as small as a drop per minute under suitable test conditions, potentially catching problems behind walls or around plumbing connections before they become severe. ￼
3. Alerts you wherever you are
Receive notifications about potential leaks and unusual water use through the app, so you can respond even when you're not home. ￼
4. Gives you remote control
You can turn your home's water supply on or off through the app, which is convenient when traveling or responding to a suspected leak. ￼
5. Helps identify wasted water
Flo tracks water usage and flow patterns, helping you spot things like running toilets, unusual consumption, or other plumbing issues that can increase your water bill. ￼
6. May help with homeowners insurance
Some insurance companies offer discounts for approved leak-detection and automatic shutoff systems. Eligibility and savings depend on your insurer and policy.

Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. During my evaluation, I found the main electrical panel to be zinsco panel. Zinsco panels were recalled in the early 1980s due to known fire hazards associated with the breakers failing to trip properly. When breakers do not trip as designed, excessive heat can build up in the breakers, wiring, and connected equipment, creating a potential fire hazard.

Due to the age and safety concerns associated with this panel, replacement of the main electrical panel is strongly recommended. These panels are considered unsafe, and replacement breakers and components may no longer be readily available if an existing breaker fails.

I also found several three-prong receptacles that are not properly grounded. Ungrounded three-prong outlets do not provide the intended equipment-grounding protection and can present a safety hazard. In the event of an electrical fault, exposed metal components or equipment could potentially become energized. The homeowner said he will adress the outlets.

I recommend replacing the existing two-prong and ungrounded receptacles with properly installed GFCI-protected receptacles, as applicable, to improve safety and bring the electrical system into compliance with current requirements where permitted.

The exterior electrical service is approximately 30 years old or older. I did not observe any immediate issues with the exterior service during today’s inspection. I did advise the homeowner that if the complete electrical service is replaced, a 10-year warranty would be provided. If only the necessary repairs are performed without replacing the complete service, the warranty would be limited to one year.

A water softener can make a big difference in your home, especially if you have hard water with high levels of calcium and magnesium. It removes those minerals through a process called ion exchange, helping reduce mineral buildup throughout your plumbing and appliances.
7 benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale and mineral buildup
Helps prevent the white, chalky deposits that accumulate on faucets, showerheads, glass shower doors, and sinks. It can also reduce scale buildup inside pipes.
2. Helps appliances last longer
Reducing scale can help protect water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other water-using appliances. It may also improve water-heater efficiency when scale would otherwise accumulate.
3. Easier cleaning
Less mineral residue means less scrubbing of shower doors, tubs, sinks, and fixtures. You may also spend less on products designed to remove hard-water deposits.
4. Better soap and detergent performance
Soap and detergent lather more easily in softened water. You may need less laundry detergent, dishwashing detergent, and body wash to get the results you want.
5. Softer-feeling laundry
Towels and clothes may feel less stiff or rough, and mineral deposits on fabrics can be reduced.
6. A smoother skin and hair feel
Some people notice less of a dry or filmy feeling after showering. However, a softener does not treat skin conditions, and individual results vary.
7. Potential long-term savings
Less scale, improved appliance performance, and reduced cleaning needs may save money over time, particularly in homes with very hard water.

e.344271519:
LPH arrived at the residence to evaluate the existing electrical system and discuss recommended improvements to enhance electrical safety, reliability, and protection throughout the home.

Basement Trough and Disconnect Replacement:

Upon inspection, LPH identified extensive rust and corrosion within the existing basement electrical trough, indicating a history of water intrusion and moisture exposure. The moisture has affected the wiring connections, leaving a film of oxidation and corrosion on the connection points and lugs. Corroded connections can increase electrical resistance, generate excessive heat, and compromise the reliability of the electrical system.

Additionally, the disconnect supplying the upstairs bedroom electrical panel has exceeded its recommended service life and shows considerable rust and corrosion throughout the enclosure. The internal lugs have also developed oxidation and corrosion, further compromising the integrity of the electrical connections. This disconnect contains a discontinued Zinsco breaker, a product line widely associated with serious safety concerns, including breakers that may fail to trip during an overload or short circuit, overheating, and connections that can deteriorate over time. These concerns can increase the risk of electrical fires and may also create complications during insurance reviews or real estate transactions.

LPH recommends replacing the existing trough and disconnect arrangement with a new electrical trough mounted securely to a backer board. The existing wiring will be reconnected using heavy-duty Polaris insulated connectors, providing secure, reliable connections. A new 100-amp disconnect will also be installed on the backer board to supply the upstairs electrical panel. This replacement will eliminate the deteriorated equipment and outdated disconnect, improve the integrity of the electrical connections, and provide a safer, more dependable electrical distribution setup.

Whole-Home Surge Protection:

During the inspection, LPH also identified deterioration affecting the electronic driver components of the arc-fault circuit interrupter (AFCI) breaker in the upstairs electrical panel. This is the only AFCI breaker currently installed in the home. Electronic components can experience wear and deterioration over time from transient voltage spikes that occur throughout a home’s electrical system. These voltage fluctuations can be generated when motor-driven equipment, such as air conditioners, refrigerators, and other appliances, cycles on and off. Utility-related disturbances and lightning can also introduce damaging voltage surges.

LPH recommends installing a premium whole-home surge protector at the electrical service equipment. This device helps limit damaging transient overvoltages before they reach connected circuits and sensitive electronic equipment. By reducing exposure to these voltage spikes, whole-home surge protection can help protect appliance control boards, televisions, computers, and other valuable electronics, potentially extending their service life and reducing the likelihood of costly premature failures. While no surge protector can eliminate every electrical threat, this upgrade provides an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical system and connected equipment.

Exterior Receptacle Safety Improvements:

During the evaluation, LPH discovered that the exterior receptacles lack GFCI protection and that two of the existing receptacles have improper covers. The receptacles currently installed are intended for indoor use and have deteriorated significantly from prolonged exposure to outdoor conditions. Moisture intrusion and corrosion can compromise receptacle connections, increase the likelihood of electrical failures, and create potential shock hazards.

LPH recommends replacing the affected exterior receptacles with weather-resistant devices designed for outdoor applications. The proposed improvements include one weather-resistant receptacle, three weather-resistant GFCI receptacles, and two extra-duty in-use bubble covers. GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of serious electrical shock by quickly interrupting power when a ground fault is detected. The weather-resistant receptacles and properly rated covers will provide improved protection against rain, moisture, and environmental exposure. The in-use bubble covers are designed to help protect receptacles while cords are plugged in, providing an additional layer of protection against water intrusion.

These improvements will address the deteriorated exterior devices, bring the receptacle installations closer to current safety expectations, and provide more dependable outdoor electrical service.

LPH recommends completing these improvements to address the existing corrosion, eliminate the outdated Zinsco disconnect, improve electrical connection reliability, and add protection against electrical shock and damaging voltage surges. Together, these upgrades will help improve the overall safety, reliability, and long-term performance of the home’s electrical system.

i.330764644: This morning I arrived at the Mentzer family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. The one recommendation I had was regarding the main electrical service. The panel appears to be in good physical condition with no signs of rusting, corrosion, or burning. However, the panel has eclipsed what we would deem to be the average life expectancy for breaker panels. The panel is over 40 years old now. As panels age, the safety features within their breakers can begin to fail to function in the event of an electrical fault. Separate from this, should any breakers fail, or need to be replaced, it can be difficult to find replacements as they do not manufacture these parts anymore. Secondary to this, the outside meterbase, and subsequently its service wiring are also exhibiting signs of age, with the service wire the primary focus. It has started to dry rot, and sun burn, which can ultimately allow for failures in its weatherproofing. this allows for moisture and other contaminants to damage the breaker panel. For these listed reasons, I have provided a primary option for the replacement of the full main electrical service. I have provided a separate option to replace two double tapped breakers with their appropriate counterparts. if you have any questions, or concerns, please do not hesitate to contact us. i.331406411:
This afternoon I arrived at the Ternoski family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon my arrival, Mr. Ternoski informed me that they had accidentally overloaded the circuit which they are using to supply power to their RV. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the circuit I do un there to be no tripped breakers, and all breaker were providing 120v of power (at minimum), yet no power was reaching the garage. I began to conduct a very thorough analysis of all devices, both known and unknown, that could potentially be on this circuit. I found no discrepancies. From there I entered the homes crawl space which spans the homes entire footprint minus the garage. I located the entry from most of the homes circuits to the breaker panel and found several discrepancies. I found improper and unsafe Junctioning means, including open junctions and splices, improperly located and unweatherized “in-wall” splices free hanging. More concerning yet, I noted that the homes dryer vent is vented almost directly onto these improper junctions. What this has done is created a thick film of dryer lint on these already potentially hazardous junctions. I have included photos of my findings, and provided an option to essentially dismantle, and properly reinstall all of these non code-compliant splices. 

Circling back to the loss of power, after digging through several of the junctions, I identified one bundle of wires which had too many hot wires under one wire nut. It appeared that one wire had been worked loose of the wire nut, and potentially further loosened during our overload event. I retracted this circuit and worked out which wires were live from the bundle in order to separate the cluster of wires properly using appropriately sized wire nuts. I was able to restore power to the garage, and also identified that the garage was being powered by a breaker labeled as “master bedroom”.

Finally I provided an estimate to run an appropriate dedicated 30A circuit and plug for the RV, as to avoid potential overloads down the road. 

If you have any questions, concerns, or if you would like to move forward with any of today’s provided estimates, please do not hesitate to reach out. Thank you for your patience today, and I look forward to our next visit!

Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. Upon evaluation, the main electrical panel was found to be in good condition. There were no signs of rust or corrosion, all electrical connections were tight, and there were no indications of overheating at the breakers.

All other electrical components throughout the home were tested and were found to be functioning properly.

However, I did identify an issue with the home’s grounding and bonding system. The grounding system consists of two primary components: the grounding electrode system (ground rods) and the bonding of the home’s metal water and gas piping.

The required bonding connection from the main electrical panel to the water piping is currently missing. A properly sized copper bonding conductor should be installed from the main electrical panel to the appropriate locations on the water piping, including the house and street sides of the water meter, with the gas piping properly bonded as required.

Proper bonding helps ensure that metal piping, gas appliances, water fixtures, and other conductive components throughout the home remain at the same electrical potential and provides a safe path for fault current back to the electrical system.

As the system currently stands, there is a potential shock hazard in the event of an electrical fault involving the gas piping, water piping, appliances, or other metal components.

Recommended Solution

Provide and install the required bonding connections to properly bond the home’s water and gas piping to the electrical grounding system and bring the system into proper compliance.

A proposal/invoice for the recommended bonding work has been provided by email for review.

e.345311548:
A water softener is a system that removes the minerals responsible for hard water, primarily calcium and magnesium. If you're considering a soft water system for your city water supply, it can make a noticeable difference in your plumbing, appliances, cleaning routine, and bathing experience.
One important distinction: city water and soft water are not the same thing. City water is treated by your municipal water utility to meet drinking-water standards, but it can still contain substantial amounts of calcium and magnesium. A home water softener reduces those minerals before the water flows through your house.
The major benefits of a water softener
1. Less scale buildup on faucets, showers, and fixtures
Hard water leaves chalky white deposits on showerheads, faucets, glass shower doors, and sinks. Soft water dramatically reduces these mineral deposits, so your bathroom and kitchen stay cleaner and require less scrubbing.
2. Longer life for household appliances
Mineral scale can accumulate inside water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other water-using appliances. Softening can reduce that buildup, help maintain efficiency, and potentially extend equipment life, particularly in areas with very hard water.
3. Softer-feeling skin after showering
Hard water can leave mineral residue on your skin. Soft water reduces that residue and may help some people feel less dry or tight after bathing. It does not treat skin conditions, and results vary by person.
4. Hair that feels easier to manage
With fewer mineral deposits left on your hair, you may notice less residue, improved softness, and easier combing. The effect depends on your hair type, products, and the hardness of your original water.
5. Cleaner dishes and glassware
Soft water helps prevent cloudy spots and white mineral film on glasses, plates, and silverware. You may also be able to reduce dishwasher detergent and rinse-aid use, following your appliance manufacturer's instructions.
6. Softer laundry and towels
Hard-water minerals can interfere with detergents and leave residue in fabrics. Soft water can help towels feel softer, clothes look brighter, and laundry rinse more effectively.
7. More lather from soap and shampoo
Calcium and magnesium react with soap and reduce its effectiveness. Soft water allows soap, shampoo, and body wash to lather more easily, so you may need less product to get the same result.
8. Better water-heater performance
Hard-water scale can build up on heating elements and inside tanks. Reducing scale may improve heat transfer and help prevent maintenance problems. The amount of energy saved depends on how hard your water is and the condition and type of your water heater.
9. Less time spent cleaning
You will generally spend less time removing hard-water rings, soap scum, and mineral crust from bathroom fixtures, shower doors, sinks, and tubs. Existing heavy deposits may still need to be cleaned off first.
10. Less soap scum in bathrooms
Soft water reduces the formation of insoluble soap deposits caused by hard-water minerals. This can mean less sticky film on tubs, shower walls, and shower curtains.
11. Reduced mineral buildup in plumbing
A properly sized and maintained softener can reduce scale inside pipes, valves, and plumbing fixtures. This is especially useful where hard water would otherwise cause substantial buildup over time. It does not repair existing corrosion or remove every type of plumbing deposit.
12. Potential savings on household products
Because soft water makes cleaning products and soaps work more effectively, you may spend less on laundry detergent, dishwashing products, shampoo, and soap. Your savings depend on your current water hardness, product use, and the cost of maintaining the softener.

Suggested to immediately contact a chimney company to inspect chimney and install a liner to help improve draft quality on the system. Also verified water pressure is within a safe threshold. While water pressure tested 75 PSI today, plumbing system is currently a closed loop system and does not allow any cushion for pressure spikes. Suggested installation of an expansion tank near the main water supply to ensure water pressure does not go above the 80 PSI danger threshold for pressure. 

Also found two other concerns during inspection today. Found some pin-holes and leaks at the main sewer stack in the basement. Lastly, identified aging and deteriorated parts inside the toilet tank upstairs.

I noticed that the home does not have whole-home surge protection installed. After speaking with the homeowner, I learned that the property experiences frequent power interruptions, even if only for short periods. Whole-home surge protection helps protect sensitive electronics and major appliances from voltage surges. These surges can originate from the utility company during power fluctuations, storms, or power restoration, as well as from within the home when large appliances, such as refrigerators and air conditioning compressors, cycle on and off. Installing a surge protection device at the electrical panel can help protect the home’s electrical equipment from damaging voltage spikes.

2. Expired Smoke Detectors
I also noticed that the home’s smoke detectors have expired. Smoke detectors generally need to be replaced every 10 years, or according to the manufacturer’s specified service life, to help ensure proper operation and reliable fire detection. I recommended replacing all expired smoke detectors.

The gas piping system does not appear to be properly bonded. Proper bonding helps reduce the risk of electrical shock by providing a path for fault current. The appropriate bonding method and connection points should be verified to ensure compliance with applicable electrical codes and manufacturer requirements. I recommended correcting this issue to improve electrical safety throughout the home.

4. Loose Bathroom Outlet
I found a loose receptacle in the bathroom, likely due to age and frequent use. A loose outlet can create an unsafe connection and should be secured or replaced as necessary. I presented the homeowner with the option to replace the existing duplex receptacle.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 19 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be 1.0 ppm. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater to allow for efficient integration into the home’s main water distribution system. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the existing main drain located behind the water heater at the proposed installation area. An outlet is provided. i.337135276: Out to home today for the yearly plumbing system check. Upon arrival to home, there were two concerns. First concern has to do with the main water shutoff valves. Homeowner states they noticed moisture near the valves and would like extra attention during visit today. The next concern has to do with a rust color in the water supply. They especially notice the rust in the bathtub upstairs. Upon evaluation, found that there was no current moisture on the main water shutoff valves. Valves appears to be in poor condition and should be replaced. During visit, LPH found two things that will cause rust in the water supply. Right at the main valves there is a small section of galvanized steel piping. Steel piping will rust from the inside and leech into the water. When the water softener is active, it will filter out trace amounts of iron. Found the water softener does not have any salt and is not filtering very well. These factors combine to cause trace iron in the water supply. Suggested best solution is to replace the main shut off valves and remove the galvanized piping. From there, performed full home plumbing inspection. Performed flush of water heater and tested water pressure. No other concerns were found during visit. Went over recommendations for the main valve. Pricing provided today is valid for 60 days. Thank you for trusting LPH.

e.341722344:

Directly after the valves, there is a small section of galvanized steel piping that is leeching iron and rust through water supply. Since the water softener is not working properly due to a lack of salt, iron is getting into the water supply and all throughout the home. During replacement of main shut off valves, LPH will remove section of galvanized and replace with stainless steel/brass then reconnect into the copper.

Out to home today for the yearly plumbing system check. Upon arrival to home, there were two main concerns. Home is experiencing backups and slow drainage from the laundry, shower, and lavatory sink in the basement of the home. Upon inspection, identified that the issue is relating to improper venting and slow buildup. Confirmed the issue is not relating to the main drain. The toilet in the downstairs bathroom, floor drain, and kitchen sink are all working properly at this time. Suggested best solution is to install a mechanical air vent and perform a drain cleaning service for branch lines. The next concern has to do with the main water shut off valve. Homeowner states the current main valve is not very accessible and is requesting pricing on relocating the valves. Upon inspection of valves, confirmed the valves are old and unreliable. Suggested replacement of main shut off valves and relocating the secondary valve to an accessible location in the utility room. 

From there, performed the full home plumbing inspection. Performed flush of water heater system. Tested water pressure to be within a safe threshold for inside the home. Performed water quality test and found high hardness and chlorine in the water. Suggested corrective measures for water quality to protect the home, plumbing, and occupants of the home. 

Found several other concerns during visit today. In the utility room, identified the laundry faucet is leaking down through sink on concrete floor. Kitchen faucet upstairs is loose and in poor condition. Also in the upstairs bathroom, the tub spout is faulty and not diverting the water properly.

Went over all suggestions and recommendations based on the plumbing inspection today. Homeowner approved the drain rebuild and drain cleaning service today. Scheduled to return Tuesday October 6th first stop to complete requested services and repairs. Collected a 30% deposit for work to be completed. Remainder of balance to be collected upon completion of services. All other pricing provided today is valid for 60 days. Thank you for trusting LPH.

Out to home today for the yearly plumbing system check. Upon arrival to home, there were two concerns in regards to the plumbing. 

First concern has to do with requesting pricing on installation of a new drinking water system. They currently have one installed, however the unit is disconnected and not functioning. They would like a new one installed and then have a line connected to the existing faucet and over to the fridge. 
Second concern has to do with the powder room sink. They had jewelry fall down the drain. They took apart the drain and was able to retrieve the lost item. They are requesting for the sink to be reconnected under neath. Upon evaluation, found that the pop-up drain is old and corroded and should be replaced as well. Provided solution of replacing pop-up drain and reconnecting sink. 

From there, performed the full home plumbing inspection today. During inspection, performed routine flush of water heater system. Performed water quality test and verified function of softener system. Also tested water pressure to be within a safe threshold inside the home at about 60 PSI. 

Found several concerns during the inspection today. 

At the kitchen sink, found that the garbage disposal is not working and over 10 years old. The kitchen faucet leaks from the base and down into the cabinet below. The old drainage is corroded and there is an open hole in the drop where the old RO drained into. In the powder room, found a leak coming from the tank of the toilet. In the full bathroom at the front of the home, the toilet is out of commission due to a previous leak. They stated that the toilet had been shut off for about 3 years. LPH will need to perform major rebuild of toilet tank and reset seal from base of fixture. Recommended replacement of fixture due to condition. In both upstairs bathrooms, the tub spout leaks quite a bit when running the shower reducing quantity and volume of hot water during showers. 

In the Basement, found that the water softener unit is extremely aged being installed back in 2001. Suggested replacement of unit due to being over the expected lifespan for the system. Found whole home expansion tank to have failed and is not able to react and absorb changes to water pressure. This will cause pressure spikes inside the home and lead to failure of plumbing components. At the water heater system, the condensation drains onto the floor then into a ground water pit. Suggested rerouting condensate into pump system to discharge into the sewer. Lastly, the outdoor faucets on the back and front of the home leaks when in use. 

Went over all recommendations and pricing for repairs. Pricing provided today is valid for 60 days. 

If you found value in the inspection today, LPH highly recommends signing up for our membership program to have these inspections performed every year. Left information behind about plan. i.339318239:
Today, I arrived at the Themis residence to perform a complimentary electrical system check. Upon arrival, the homeowner informed me of several electrical concerns she wanted me to evaluate, including an issue with the dryer and a dining room light that was not functioning properly.

Upon evaluating the dryer, I found that the dryer itself appears to have an internal failure or a failed component, which is causing it not to operate properly. The issue does not appear to be related to the home’s electrical supply.

The homeowner also reported that the dining room light had stopped working after she reset the breaker. I proceeded to the electrical panel to inspect the breakers, voltages, and connections. Upon inspection, I found that both 200-amp main electrical panels are enclosed within a cabinet and are currently inaccessible because they are completely stuck within the cabinet.

The two main electrical panels are original to the home and are over 35 years old. Due to their age, there is an increased likelihood of breaker and other component failures, which can contribute to electrical distribution problems and potential safety concerns. The panels are Sylvania panels, which are known to have issues with breakers failing to trip properly under certain fault conditions. A breaker that fails to trip when required can allow excessive current to continue flowing, potentially resulting in overheating or damage to connected electrical components.

Based on the age, condition, accessibility, and manufacturer of the existing equipment, I informed homeowner both 200-amp main electrical panels need to be replaced to improve electrical safety, reliability, and proper power distribution throughout the home.

I also explained that the existing cabinet will need to be modified or removed as necessary to provide proper access when the panels are replaced. In addition, surge protection will need to be installed at the main panels as part of the panel replacement to meet current code requirements. Themis didn’t want anything els checked during today visit.

An estimate/solution was presented to the homeowner. She stated that she would discuss the recommended work with her daughter and get back to us regarding how she would like to proceed. 
Thank you for letting us ensure safety to your home.

The Moen Flo Smart Water Monitor and Shutoff is a smart-home device that monitors your home's water use and can automatically shut off the main water supply if it detects a potential leak. Its biggest benefit is helping protect your home from costly water damage, even when you're away.
The 7 biggest benefits of a Moen Flo
1. Automatic leak detection and shutoff
Flo learns your home's water-use patterns and looks for unusual activity, such as a possible burst pipe or continuous water flow. When it identifies a qualifying leak, it can automatically shut off the water to help limit damage.
2. Protection against expensive water damage
A failed washing machine hose, leaking toilet, broken pipe, or other plumbing problem can cause damage to flooring, drywall, cabinets, and personal belongings. Catching a problem early can potentially save thousands of dollars.
3. Alerts on your phone
Get notifications about unusual water activity and potential leaks, so you can respond even when you're at work, traveling, or away from home.
4. Track water consumption
Monitor water usage, identify changes in your household's consumption, and spot possible waste that might otherwise go unnoticed.
5. Detect hidden plumbing problems
Small leaks and running toilets can go unnoticed for days or weeks. Flo's monitoring can help identify abnormal water use that may point to an issue.
6. Peace of mind while traveling
You can check your water system remotely and, depending on the alert and device operation, shut off the water without needing to return home first.
7. Potential insurance benefits
Some insurers may offer discounts or other benefits for approved water-leak prevention devices. Eligibility varies by insurer, policy, and device, so confirm before buying.

LPH performed a comprehensive electrical system check to evaluate the condition, safety, and reliability of the home’s electrical components. During the inspection, the homeowner’s concerns regarding nonfunctioning electrical devices led to further investigation, revealing extensive deterioration and potentially dangerous conditions throughout the home.

Switches and Receptacles: Upon opening device boxes and examining the existing wiring connections, LPH discovered widespread damage associated with the existing backstab wiring method. Nearly every device inspected showed significant deterioration, including heat-related cracking, broken device housings, loose conductors, and electrical arcing. In some instances, minimal movement while inspecting the devices caused components to break apart, wires to short together, and arcing to occur. During today’s system check, LPH identified 22 single-pole switches, 7 three-way switches, 5 duplex receptacles, and 1 dimmer switch exhibiting serious damage or unsafe connections. Due to the extent of the deterioration, LPH recommends replacing all switches and duplex receptacles throughout the home rather than limiting repairs to devices that have already failed. Devices that appear intact externally may still have compromised internal connections, and additional devices may be affected because not every device box could be opened and inspected within the available timeframe.

Kitchen GFCI Protection: LPH identified a failed GFCI receptacle protecting the kitchen countertop circuit. The device is no longer tripping as intended, leaving the portion of the circuit it protects without functioning ground-fault protection. Replacement is recommended to restore this important protection against electrical shock.

Exterior Meter Base and Service Cable: LPH also evaluated concerns regarding possible water intrusion at the exterior meter base. Small amounts of water intrusion were suspected within the meter base enclosure. Visible rust was present along one side of the electrical panel, and corrosion was observed on the service cable near its outer jacket. These findings raise concerns regarding continued moisture exposure and potential deterioration of the electrical service components. LPH recommends inspecting and resealing the exterior meter base entry points with appropriate exterior-rated sealant and replacing the existing service cable between the meter base and interior electrical panel. The accessible service equipment and cable entry points should also be inspected for additional moisture-related damage, with the electrical service tested upon completion of the repairs.

Immediate Safety Repairs: Due to the severity of the damaged electrical connections identified during the inspection, one three-way switch was approved by the homeowner for immediate replacement today because leaving the damaged device connected presented an imminent electrical safety concern. The remaining recommendations address additional hazards and proactive improvements intended to reduce the risk of overheating, electrical arcing, electrical shock, and potential fire.

Estimates and Follow-Up: LPH reviewed the findings and recommendations identified during today’s system check. The homeowner approved the immediate replacement of the damaged three-way switch. A Moen Flo is a smart water leak detection and automatic shutoff system that helps protect your home from costly water damage. Think of it as a security system for your home's plumbing: it monitors your water 24/7 and can automatically turn off the main water supply when it detects a potential serious leak.

1. Helps prevent expensive water damage
If a pipe bursts, a supply line breaks, or water runs abnormally, Flo can detect the problem and shut off the main water supply to limit flooding. This can be particularly valuable when you're sleeping or away on vacation.
2. Detects hidden leaks
Its daily MicroLeak tests can identify leaks as small as approximately one drop per minute. That may help you catch a slow leak behind a wall or from a plumbing fixture before it causes major damage. ￼
3. Sends alerts to your phone
You can receive notifications about unusual water usage and possible leaks, helping you respond quickly whether you're at home, at work, or traveling.
4. Lets you monitor water usage
See water consumption, flow rate, pressure, and usage history. This can help identify a running toilet, an unnoticed leak, or other unnecessary water consumption.
5. Provides peace of mind while traveling
You can check your home's water system remotely and turn the water off through the app. Automatic shutoff can be especially useful if a leak occurs while no one is home.
6. May help with insurance costs
Some insurance companies offer discounts for qualifying leak-prevention systems. Eligibility and savings depend on your insurer and policy, so check before purchasing.

i.340066220:
LPH arrived at the home to perform a comprehensive electrical system check and discuss the homeowners’ future plans for the property. During the evaluation, we reviewed the existing electrical system, discussed current concerns, and explored several improvements to help accommodate the homeowners’ planned basement renovations and future electrical needs.

Basement Electrical Rewiring and Future Improvements

We discussed the existing basement electrical layout, which currently relies heavily on a single circuit supplying the basement lighting and receptacles, exterior receptacles, screened-in porch receptacles, and kitchen island receptacle. With the planned basement improvements, including a kitchenette, exercise area, fireplace heater, radon fan, and inflatable hot tub, adding dedicated circuits and redistributing the existing electrical loads will provide a more functional electrical layout and help reduce the likelihood of nuisance tripping.

LPH provided an estimate to rewire the unfinished basement with six new circuits, including dedicated circuits for the radon fan, exercise equipment, kitchenette, fireplace heater, exterior hot tub, and general basement receptacles. The proposed work also includes transferring the upstairs kitchen island receptacle to the new kitchenette circuit, installing the appropriate AFCI/GFCI protection, and transitioning the existing wiring through accessible junction boxes to maintain continuity for the remaining circuits.

We also discussed adding a new 20-amp circuit from the main electrical panel to provide receptacles inside the garage and outside the home. This will provide a more appropriate power source for the garage microwave and eliminate the need to rely on an extension cord plugged into the garage door opener receptacle.

Exterior Receptacle Repairs and Whole-Home Surge Protection

During our discussion, we reviewed the condition of the existing exterior receptacles and the importance of maintaining proper weather protection and GFCI protection in outdoor locations. LPH provided an estimate to replace the damaged receptacles with new weather-resistant devices, including two weather-resistant GFCI receptacles and two weather-resistant duplex receptacles, utilizing the existing appropriate bubble covers.

We also discussed installing whole-home surge protection to help protect sensitive electronics, appliances, and other electrical equipment from damaging voltage surges originating from utility disturbances, lightning-related events, and electrical equipment cycling within the home. This additional protection is particularly beneficial when investing in new electrical equipment and modern circuit protection.

Grounding and Bonding Improvements

We discussed the existing grounding and bonding system, which requires additional attention to address the incomplete grounding arrangement. LPH provided an additional estimate to install an appropriate grounding clamp and connection at the existing metal water line, where applicable, and add approximately five feet of grounding conductor to bond the home’s gas piping system as required by applicable electrical code.

Proper grounding and bonding help establish an intentional path for electrical fault current and reduce potentially dangerous voltage differences between metal piping systems and other grounded components throughout the home.

Main Electrical Panel Replacement

We also discussed the existing 200-amp Crouse-Hinds electrical panel, which is approximately 34 years old. Although the panel is rated for 200 amps, its age warrants consideration of replacement as the homeowners continue making improvements to the property and adding electrical loads.

LPH provided a separate estimate to replace the existing panel with a new 42-space Eaton CH panel. This upgrade will provide modern electrical distribution equipment, additional circuit spaces for future projects, and an opportunity to evaluate the existing service connections, breaker connections, grounding, bonding, and neutral terminations.

Replacing the panel proactively will help improve long-term serviceability and provide a better foundation for the home’s future electrical needs. We also discussed incorporating whole-home surge protection as part of the overall electrical improvement plan.

Review of Options and Plans Moving Forward

All recommendations and available options were discussed with the homeowner in relation to the property’s current electrical conditions and the planned basement improvements. Separate estimates have been prepared to allow the homeowners to review the proposed work, compare the options, and determine how they would like to proceed.

We will carve out time tomorrow morning to fully discuss the estimates, answer any remaining questions, prioritize the recommended improvements, and determine the best plan moving forward.

Today’s electrical system check evaluation and all associated estimates will be emailed to the homeowners for their review.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate the opportunity to evaluate your electrical system and discuss your future plans for the property. We look forward to speaking with you tomorrow morning and servicing you again in the future.
