e.344691385:
Electrical Panel Replacement – Crouse-Hinds Panel

Reason for Replacement

LPH recommends replacing the existing 42-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel due to its age and visible signs of deterioration. The panel has exceeded its typical service life, and several concerning conditions were identified during the electrical evaluation.

Signs of rust were observed on several breakers, along with heat discoloration above the main breaker. These conditions can indicate deterioration and potential overheating within the electrical panel. Additionally, the original breakers were noticeably loose in their connections. When the breakers were gently moved, a light amount of electrical arcing could be heard, raising concerns about the integrity of the breaker-to-bus connections and the potential for unreliable electrical contact.

As electrical panels and their components age, connections can loosen, contact surfaces can deteriorate, and corrosion can develop. These conditions can increase electrical resistance, generate excessive heat, and contribute to electrical arcing. If left unaddressed, deteriorated connections can damage the panel and breakers while increasing the potential for electrical failure or fire.

Due to the age of the panel, rust on the breakers, heat discoloration, and audible arcing associated with movement of the original breakers, LPH recommends replacing the existing electrical panel rather than continuing to rely on deteriorated equipment.

Installing a new electrical panel will provide modern electrical distribution equipment, new breakers, and properly established connections to improve the safety and reliability of the home’s electrical system.

Scope of Work Includes:

* Remove the existing 42-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel.
* Transfer and properly terminate the existing branch circuits.
* Install new breakers appropriate for the existing circuits and new panel.
* Inspect existing branch-circuit wiring for signs of damage or deterioration at accessible connection points.
* Properly establish neutral and grounding connections in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements.
* Inspect and verify electrical terminations and connections.
* Properly label the new electrical panel and individual circuits.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation of the electrical system.

Benefits of Replacing the Existing Panel

Improved Electrical Safety: Replacing the aging panel addresses concerns associated with deteriorated equipment, rust, heat discoloration, and loose breaker connections. New equipment and properly established connections help reduce the risks associated with overheating and electrical arcing.

Reliable Breaker Connections: The original breakers have become noticeably loose, and movement produced audible arcing. A new panel with compatible breakers will provide new breaker mounting and contact components, helping establish reliable electrical connections.

Reduced Risk of Overheating: Rust and heat discoloration are warning signs that warrant attention. Replacing the panel allows the affected equipment to be removed and the connected wiring to be inspected for damage before being terminated in the new panel.

Modern Electrical Distribution: A new 42-space Eaton CH panel provides a modern electrical distribution system designed to accommodate compatible breakers and support the home’s electrical needs.

Future Electrical Flexibility: The new panel provides additional circuit spaces for potential future electrical additions, subject to the available service capacity and the home’s calculated electrical load.

Peace-of-Mind Warranty

Your new Eaton CH electrical panel and breakers are protected by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while maintaining an active LPH Service Partner Plan (SPP) membership, providing continued coverage and added peace of mind.

Long-Term Value

Replacing the existing Crouse-Hinds panel is a proactive investment in the safety and reliability of the home’s electrical system. With the panel approximately 42 years old and showing signs of rust, heat discoloration, loose breaker connections, and audible arcing, continuing to rely on the existing equipment presents avoidable concerns.

A new electrical panel will replace the deteriorated components, provide properly established breaker connections, and help restore dependable electrical distribution throughout the home.

All work will be completed in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements and the requirements of the local authority having jurisdiction.

i.344438086:
This afternoon I arrived at the Lippart family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. The one recommendation I had was regarding the main breaker panel. The panel appears to be in good physical condition with no signs of rusting, corrosion, or burning. However, the panel has eclipsed what we would deem to be the average life expectancy for breaker panels. The panel is over 40 years old now. As panels age, the safety features within their breakers can begin to fail to function in the event of an electrical fault. Separate from this, should any breakers fail, or need to be replaced, it can be difficult to find replacements as they do not manufacture these parts anymore. 
LPH also noticed that the appliances in the home are missing active surge protection to defend against any spike of voltage that can enter/be produced inside of the home and potentially damage motherboards or other electrical components inside appliances. A whole home surge protection device that gets mounted and connected at the panel will help defend against these harmful spikes of voltage. The device installed will come with lifetime parts warranty and up to $100,000 of repair or replacement(whichever is less) coverage in the event that a grounded appliance/equipment(the appliance/equipment that come with a home such as A/C, Furnace, other home intergraded heating system(boilers and water heaters), water purification system, range, microwave, refrigerator, and etc.) becomes damaged due to a surge with this device installed. *Whole home surge protection device is NOT a power conditioner, meaning that the home surge device will not eliminate the minor flickering for bulbs entirely but will alleviate most of the major/noticeable flickering/strobbing*. I provided estimates to replace the full electrical service, separately the panel alone, and lastly to install a whole home surge protection device. IF you have any questions or would like to move forward with any of these estimates please do not hesitate to reach out! Thank you.

i.344498603:
Homeowner showed the technician the condensation pump located in the basement at the Bosch furnace installed by LPH. Homeowner explained that the condensation pump had been experiencing intermittent issues with turning on and/or keeping up with the amount of condensation being produced. During these occurrences, the thermostat would display an error indicating that the system was waiting for the unit. LPH previously replaced the thermostat twice without resolving the issue. LPH also replaced the condensation pump twice; however, the problem continued to occur, most recently the previous week while the air conditioning system was running.

Technician connected a hose to the boiler drain at the well pressure tank to introduce water into the condensation pump and simulate the drainage from two units running simultaneously. During testing, technician observed that the condensation pump was discharging water too slowly to keep up with the incoming water flow. Technician inspected the existing 3/8-inch PEX discharge tubing and determined that it was restricting the discharge flow. Technician replaced the existing 3/8-inch PEX tubing with 3/8-inch vinyl tubing. After replacing the tubing, technician tested the condensation pump again and observed improved water flow and a faster discharge rate. This correction improved the pump’s ability to remove water during testing.

Due to the ongoing nature of this issue and the previous attempts to resolve it, technician waived the dispatch fee and completed the discharge tubing replacement at no additional charge.

e.344707129:
LPH will install a new, dedicated electrical circuit from the electrical panel to the location where the oxygen pump is stationed. The oxygen pump is currently causing nuisance tripping of the brand-new arc-fault circuit breaker, which was previously replaced in September after similar issues began following the delivery of a new machine to the home.

The concern is that the oxygen pump may be contributing to the issue in two ways: the possibility of overloading the existing shared circuit with other electrical devices, or electrical interference generated by the pump’s internal condenser and electronic components that may be triggering the arc-fault breaker’s sensitive detection circuitry after approximately one hour of operation.

Installing a dedicated circuit will separate the oxygen pump from other electrical loads and help eliminate concerns associated with sharing the existing circuit. Using a standard circuit breaker, where permitted by applicable electrical code and the equipment manufacturer’s requirements, will also help address potential nuisance tripping associated with the pump’s electronic operation.

This solution is intended to provide a more reliable power source for the oxygen pump, reduce the likelihood of unexpected interruptions, and provide the homeowner with greater peace of mind when relying on this equipment.

I ran to the venting to inspect it and found a hose dripped over it, as well as the venting itself installed incorrectly. At this time I have shut off the gas to the furnace as it is unsafe to operate due to a failed heat exchanger. At this time the heat exchanger is back ordered. We are working to see what warranty credit options are available and will be out tomorrow to give pricing on replacing the furnace.

Water pressure was tested at 100 PSI, which is above the recommended residential range of 40–60 PSI. There is an existing pressure reducing valve that is no longer regulating water pressure. Excessively high water pressure can place additional stress on the home’s plumbing system and may lead to premature failure of plumbing fixtures, faucets, appliances, water heaters, and supply lines.

It is recommended to install or adjust a pressure-reducing valve (PRV) to regulate the incoming water pressure and maintain it within the recommended 40–60 PSI range. Properly regulated water pressure will help protect the plumbing system and reduce the risk of leaks, fixture damage, and premature component failure.

Technician snaked the laundry and kitchen drain due to slow drainage and the presence of an existing underground cast-iron drain line. To help improve drainage and reduce the potential for future blockages associated with the existing underground piping, Technician recommends rerouting the laundry and kitchen drain above ground. The new drain piping would connect to the existing 4-inch main waste stack, eliminating the need for the drain line to run underground. Technician also recommends installing an air admittance valve (AAV) beneath the kitchen sink to provide proper venting for the drainage system. This will help maintain proper air flow within the drain piping and improve drainage performance for both the kitchen sink and laundry tub.

Technician found that the basement laundry tub/kitchen drain was backing up and draining slowly. Technician removed the existing P-trap from the laundry tub drain and used a cable machine to clear the drain line, which runs underground and connects to the existing cast-iron piping. While cabling the drain, technician encountered an obstruction approximately 10–15 feet into the underground drain line but was able to break through and clear the blockage. Technician continued running the cable through the drain line to the full length of the cable machine, approximately 70 feet, to help ensure the line was clear.

After completing the drain cleaning, technician reinstalled the P-trap and filled the laundry tub with water twice to test the drainage. Both tests confirmed that the water drained properly without backing up, indicating that the drain was flowing freely at the time of service.

e.345154349:
LPH will rewire the unfinished basement and install six new dedicated circuits from the existing basement subpanel. This upgrade will provide properly distributed electrical service for the basement’s current and planned uses, reduce the electrical load on the existing circuits, and provide the appropriate protection for the new receptacles and connected equipment.

Basement Rewiring – Six New Circuits

1. Dedicated 15-Amp Radon Fan Circuit

* Install one new 15-amp circuit dedicated to the radon fan.
* Install a single receptacle at the designated location, with conduit piped down the wall to provide a protected wiring method.

This dedicated circuit will provide a separate power source for the radon fan rather than relying on a shared circuit serving other basement equipment and receptacles.

2. Dedicated 20-Amp Exercise Area Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit to supply the basement exercise area.
* Install three receptacles to accommodate the designated exercise equipment.
* Install two receptacles along the wall bordering the mechanical room.
* Reuse the existing conduit at the designated location, remove the existing receptacle wiring, and install new wiring and a new receptacle.

Providing a dedicated circuit for the exercise area will help accommodate the electrical demand of the equipment without adding additional loads to the general basement receptacle circuit.

3. Dedicated 20-Amp Basement Kitchenette Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit to supply the planned basement kitchenette.
* Install two receptacle locations at the designated areas.
* Pick up the upstairs kitchen island receptacle as part of this circuit using wiring accessible from the basement.

Including the upstairs kitchen island receptacle on this new circuit will help remove its load from the existing circuit serving the basement lighting, screened-in porch, and existing exterior receptacles. This will help distribute the electrical demand more appropriately and reduce the likelihood of nuisance tripping on the existing circuit.

This circuit will provide a separate power source for the kitchenette and kitchen island receptacles, helping distribute the electrical load as the basement living space is developed.

4. Dedicated 20-Amp Fireplace Heater Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit dedicated to the basement fireplace heater.
* Install one receptacle at the designated location, with conduit piped down the wall.

A dedicated circuit will help accommodate the heater’s electrical demand without unnecessarily loading the general-purpose basement receptacle circuit.

5. Dedicated 20-Amp Exterior Hot Tub Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit from the basement subpanel, routed across the basement and drilled through the exterior wall to the back porch.
* Install one weather-resistant GFCI receptacle with an appropriate in-use bubble cover to supply the 120-volt inflatable hot tub.

Because this receptacle will serve equipment used around water, proper ground-fault protection is particularly important. GFCI protection is designed to quickly interrupt power when an electrical fault creates a potentially dangerous shock hazard.

The final circuit and receptacle arrangement will need to meet the hot tub manufacturer’s electrical requirements and applicable code requirements for the installation location.

6. Dedicated 20-Amp General Basement Receptacle Circuit

* Install one new 20-amp circuit to supply the remaining designated basement receptacles.
* Reuse the existing conduit at one location and install a new receptacle.
* Cut in one receptacle along the stairway wall.
* Install three additional receptacles at the designated locations, using conduit down the block walls as needed.

This additional circuit will provide convenient receptacle access throughout the basement while distributing the electrical demand across multiple circuits instead of continuing to rely on the existing overloaded arrangement.

Basement Circuit Protection

The six new circuits will be installed from the existing basement subpanel using the appropriate wiring methods and circuit protection for their intended applications. The estimate includes:

* Four 20-amp dual-function AFCI/GFCI circuit breakers.
* One 20-amp AFCI circuit breaker.
* One 15-amp AFCI circuit breaker.

AFCI protection is designed to detect certain dangerous electrical arcing conditions that can lead to fires. GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of electrical shock by detecting ground faults and interrupting power. Dual-function breakers combine both protective features in one device.

The specified breakers will provide the intended protection for the new circuits while helping bring the installation into compliance with applicable electrical code requirements.

Existing Basement Wiring – Junction Box Transition

Currently, one existing circuit supplies the basement lighting and receptacles, exterior receptacles, screened-in porch receptacles, and kitchen island receptacle. This places a substantial number of electrical loads on a single circuit and can contribute to nuisance tripping when multiple devices are operating.

As part of this project, LPH will disconnect and transition the existing basement wiring as necessary, installing accessible junction boxes along the basement ceiling to maintain continuity for the existing circuits. This will allow the existing wiring to remain operational while the new circuits take over the designated basement receptacle loads and the upstairs kitchen island receptacle is transferred to the new kitchenette circuit.

The goal is to distribute the electrical demand more appropriately, reduce the burden on the existing circuit, and provide a more functional electrical layout for the basement and the home’s connected areas.

Whole-Home Surge Protection Recommendation

With the installation of multiple new circuits and sensitive AFCI/GFCI protective devices, LPH recommends adding a whole-home surge protector at the main electrical panel.

Modern electrical equipment, appliances, and electronic circuit boards can be damaged by voltage surges originating from utility disturbances, lightning-related events, or electrical equipment cycling on and off within the home. These events can also contribute to premature wear or damage to sensitive electronic components.

A whole-home surge protector provides an additional layer of defense by helping divert damaging transient voltage away from the home’s electrical system and connected equipment. It is particularly beneficial for homes with modern appliances, HVAC equipment, electronics, and other sensitive devices.

Although surge protection cannot prevent every type of electrical disturbance or guarantee that equipment will never be damaged, it is a worthwhile protective upgrade for the home.

Additional 20-Amp Exterior Circuit From the Main Panel

LPH will install one additional 20-amp circuit from the main electrical panel to supply two receptacles serving the main garage area: one receptacle inside the garage below the electrical panel and one exterior receptacle on the opposite side of the wall.

This installation will include:

* Routing the new circuit from the main panel and dropping down the wall to the designated locations.
* Installing a GFCI-protected receptacle at the designated exterior location.
* Installing one receptacle inside the garage below the electrical panel.
* Providing convenient power sources for both interior garage and exterior use.
* Providing a more suitable power source for the garage microwave, reducing reliance on the existing garage door opener receptacle and extension cord.

Currently, the microwave is being powered through the garage door opener receptacle using an extension cord. This is not an ideal arrangement for an appliance that draws substantial current, particularly when the circuit may already be supplying other equipment. A properly installed receptacle on a new circuit will provide a more appropriate power source and help reduce nuisance tripping caused by shared electrical loads.

Exterior Receptacle Repairs and Weather Protection

LPH will also address the damaged exterior receptacles by replacing the existing devices with new weather-resistant receptacles and providing the required GFCI protection.

This portion of the work includes:

* Two weather-resistant GFCI receptacles.
* Two weather-resistant duplex receptacles.
* Reuse of the existing boxes and appropriate bubble covers where suitable.

Weather-resistant receptacles are designed to better withstand outdoor environmental exposure. Combined with appropriate GFCI protection and suitable covers, these replacements will help reduce the risk of moisture-related deterioration, electrical faults, and shock hazards.

The existing boxes are already equipped with appropriate bubble covers, so the existing covers will be retained where they are in suitable condition and compatible with the new receptacles.

Additional Grounding and Bonding Improvements

LPH recommends completing the home’s grounding and bonding system by installing a grounding clamp on the existing metal water line and adding approximately 5 feet of grounding conductor to bond the home’s gas piping system as required by applicable electrical code.

* Water Line Grounding: Install an approved grounding clamp on the existing metal water line and connect it to the home’s grounding electrode system as appropriate. This will address the incomplete grounding arrangement and help establish the required electrical connection to the metal water piping where applicable.
* Gas Line Bonding: Install approximately 5 feet of additional grounding conductor to properly bond the home’s gas piping system to the electrical grounding system, as required by applicable code provisions.

Proper grounding and bonding help provide a safe, intentional path for fault current, allowing protective devices to operate as intended during an electrical fault. These connections also help reduce dangerous voltage differences between metal piping systems and other grounded electrical components.

Completing these improvements will help bring the home’s grounding and bonding system into compliance with applicable electrical code requirements and provide an additional layer of protection for the home’s occupants and electrical equipment.

Installation, Testing, and Completion

All new circuits will be routed from the designated electrical panels using appropriate wiring methods, conduit, junction boxes, and circuit protection for their intended applications. LPH will complete the installation in accordance with applicable electrical code requirements, verify the new connections, and test the installed devices and circuits for proper operation.

The overall goal of this project is to provide a safer, more organized, and more functional electrical system for the unfinished basement and surrounding areas. By adding dedicated circuits for the radon fan, exercise equipment, kitchenette, fireplace heater, and hot tub, transferring the upstairs kitchen island receptacle to the new kitchenette circuit, expanding general receptacle capacity, and addressing the exterior electrical concerns, LPH will help accommodate the home’s electrical needs while reducing dependence on the existing heavily loaded circuit.

LPH will replace the existing expired smoke detectors throughout the home with new smoke detectors equipped with 10-year sealed lithium battery power. This upgrade will provide the homeowner with reliable smoke detection while eliminating the need for routine battery replacements over the detectors’ service life. All new detectors will be properly installed and tested to verify operation, helping maintain dependable early-warning protection for the home and its occupants.

LPH recommends replacing the existing 34-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel with a brand-new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel while retaining the home’s existing 200-amp service capacity.

Although the existing Crouse-Hinds panel is rated for 200 amps, its age and original design make replacement a worthwhile investment in the home’s electrical safety, reliability, and ability to accommodate modern electrical demands. Electrical panels are responsible for distributing power throughout the home and providing overcurrent protection to individual circuits. As panels age, breakers and internal connection points can experience wear, deterioration, and reduced reliability. Breaker connections on the bus bar can also loosen over time, potentially causing overheating, arcing, or unreliable circuit operation.

Why Upgrade the Existing Panel?

1. Aging Electrical Equipment

At approximately 34 years old, the existing Crouse-Hinds panel has provided decades of service. However, its age warrants consideration of replacement before deterioration or component failures create a more urgent situation. Replacing the panel allows LPH to install new equipment rather than continuing to depend on aging internal components and connections.

2. Better Support for Today’s Electrical Demands

Modern homes typically place greater demands on their electrical systems than they did decades ago. Today’s households rely on larger appliances, home office equipment, entertainment systems, exercise equipment, electronic devices, and other electrical loads that may not have been anticipated when the original panel was installed.

The existing panel’s 200-amp rating does not automatically mean the home needs a larger service. However, replacing the older panel provides an opportunity to improve circuit organization, evaluate the home’s electrical distribution, and accommodate additional circuit protection and future electrical projects where capacity permits.

3. Upgrade to a New 42-Space Eaton CH Panel

LPH will replace the existing Crouse-Hinds panel with a new 42-space Eaton CH panel. This provides a modern panel assembly with additional circuit spaces to help organize the home’s electrical system and accommodate future circuit additions, subject to the available service and load capacity.

The new panel will also provide a suitable platform for compatible circuit breakers and modern protective devices as needed for the home’s electrical requirements.

4. Improved Long-Term Reliability and Serviceability

Replacing the existing panel allows LPH to evaluate the incoming service conductors, grounding and bonding connections, neutral and ground terminations, and branch-circuit connections as part of the installation. This includes inspecting the breaker connections at the bus bar for looseness, signs of overheating, or other conditions that may affect safe operation. This helps identify concerns that may otherwise remain hidden within aging equipment.

A new panel can also make future electrical maintenance and troubleshooting more straightforward by providing current, compatible equipment and a more organized circuit layout.

5. Opportunity to Incorporate Whole-Home Surge Protection

As part of the panel replacement, LPH recommends installing whole-home surge protection to help protect sensitive electronics and appliances from damaging voltage transients originating from utility disturbances, lightning-related events, and electrical equipment cycling within the home.

Modern appliances and electronic equipment contain circuit boards and sensitive components that can be vulnerable to voltage surges. Whole-home surge protection provides an additional layer of defense for the home’s electrical system and connected equipment.

Scope of Work

LPH will:

* Remove the existing 34-year-old Crouse-Hinds electrical panel.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel while maintaining the existing 200-amp service rating, provided the existing service components and installation support that configuration.
* Transfer the existing branch circuits to the new panel using compatible circuit breakers and appropriate wiring methods.
* Inspect breaker connections at the bus bar and address any loose, damaged, or overheated connections identified during the installation.
* Inspect and address grounding, bonding, neutral, and equipment grounding connections as required for the installation.
* Verify circuit identification and organize the panel directory.
* Evaluate the existing service connections and associated components for any additional concerns identified during replacement.
* Test the completed installation to verify proper operation.
* Provide whole-home surge protection as a recommended additional upgrade, if included in the approved scope.

The Long-Term Benefit

Replacing the existing Crouse-Hinds panel is a proactive investment in the home’s electrical infrastructure. Rather than waiting for aging equipment to develop a problem, the homeowner can move forward with a modern panel that offers additional circuit spaces, improved serviceability, and a better foundation for future electrical upgrades.

The goal is not simply to replace a panel because it is old. It is to update an aging, critical electrical component so the home’s distribution system is better positioned to serve the family’s current needs and future electrical demands.

i.345069621:
Technician was dispatched today to investigate a puddle of water on the left side of the chimney in the garage.

Upon inspection, the technician determined that the sewer line exits on the opposite side of the home, making it unlikely to be related to the issue. Additionally, there are no drain lines located near the chimney.

The technician found that the main water line enters the home on the right side of the chimney. Although there is a small possibility that the main water supply line could be contributing to the issue, the technician does not believe this is the most likely cause for the following reasons:

1. No indication of a continuous underground leak: The municipality has not contacted the homeowner regarding unusual water usage or a potential discrepancy between water consumption and meter readings. While this does not definitively rule out an underground leak, there is currently no known indication of one.
2. The water intrusion is intermittent: The homeowner has reported that this issue has been occurring over the past several months, but the puddle does not consistently return or progressively worsen. Because the main water line is pressurized, a leak in this line would generally be expected to produce a more continuous water loss, although the severity can vary depending on the type and location of the leak.

Based on the findings, the technician believes the issue is more likely related to the chimney or water intrusion from rain. The homeowner appears to experience the problem primarily after rainfall, and the technician observed staining along the bottom corner of the chimney. These findings suggest that water may be entering through or around the chimney.

Recommended Next Steps

We recommend having a qualified chimney professional inspect the chimney and determine whether there are any issues allowing water to enter the garage. If the chimney professional determines that the chimney is not the source of the water intrusion, further investigation of the home’s main water supply line may be necessary.

i.345114272:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, no electrical concerns were reported prior to our inspection. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, most of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. However, this panel is only receiving 120V out of the 240 V that is required to have proper functionality of this panel. We’ve identified that both the basement panel and apartment panel are receiving the same voltage issues. This voltage issue is stemming from the outside service, losing 1/2 of it hot wires, which is causing an entire building issue.

We were not able to do the full electrical system check since half the home was not receiving proper power and we couldn’t evaluate if all the systems were indeed functioning correctly at this time. We did provide two solutions to remedy the main issue that the homeowners are dealing with. They did not move forward with any options today. However, they will inform us of their decision in the future. We thank you for having us out to evaluate your system, and we look forward to servicing in the future.

i.345208376:
LPH returned to the home to complete the emergency electrical service replacement due to the severely deteriorated condition of the existing exterior electrical service. During the initial evaluation, extensive aluminum oxide corrosion was found on the main neutral conductor inside the exterior meter base, along with substantial corrosion on the meter base itself and the upper service cable. Moisture was also present around the service cable entry point, creating a serious electrical safety concern and an increased risk of service failure, voltage fluctuations, equipment damage, and potential fire hazards.

Completed Scope of Work:

* Shut down the electrical service and disconnected the existing service conductors from the utility supply.
* Removed the existing service head, upper service cables, exterior meter base, and deteriorated service conductors feeding the home.
* Installed a new meter base and a new 200-amp exterior emergency disconnect.
* Installed new PVC raceway to protect the service conductors from direct exposure to moisture, rain, and ultraviolet rays.
* Installed new 200-amp service conductors from the service head through the meter base and exterior disconnect.
* Installed new 200-amp, four-wire conductors from the exterior disconnect into the home’s main electrical panel.
* Extended and properly terminated the existing grounding conductors at the new exterior disconnect.
* Installed a new grounding bar inside the exterior disconnect to provide proper termination for the grounding conductors.
* Separated the neutral and grounding conductors within the main electrical panel and installed a new grounding bar.
* Removed the existing neutral-to-ground bonding connection in the main panel to accommodate the new exterior service disconnect configuration.
* Installed a bonding bridge on the exterior of the home to provide a proper connection point for additional grounding and bonding systems, including telephone and cable services.
* Sealed the new exterior equipment, raceway, and wall penetrations with silicone to help prevent future moisture intrusion.
* Reconnected the utility service conductors using permanent compression crimps and installed new protective covers.
* Restored power to the home and tested the electrical service to verify proper operation.

Final Testing & Completion:

LPH completed the service replacement and verified that the new electrical service was properly energized and functioning as intended. All work was tested prior to leaving the home, and the electrical system was operating properly at the time of completion.

This replacement addresses the significant corrosion and moisture-related deterioration identified during the initial evaluation while providing a new, properly protected 200-amp service configuration. The new exterior disconnect also provides an accessible means of shutting off power to the home from outside.

Payment was collected for the completed services. Today’s invoice will be emailed to the homeowners. Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure working with you, and we look forward to servicing you again in the future.

The homeowner should weigh the cost of leak detection, repairs, and refrigerant recharging against the investment in a new HVAC system. A new system may offer improved energy efficiency, greater reliability, and new manufacturer and labor warranty coverage, depending on the equipment selected and applicable warranty terms.

LPH Recommendation:

LPH recommends reviewing both repair and replacement options to determine the most cost-effective long-term solution for the homeowner. A comfort consultation will help compare the available options based on upfront costs, energy efficiency, expected reliability, and long-term operating expenses.

i.345288232: This afternoon I arrived at the Sellers family home to conduct their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies. The one recommendation I had was regarding the main breaker panel. The panel appears to be in okay physical condition with some signs of rusting/ corrosion, but no or burning arcing. However, the panel is nearing what we would deem to be the average life expectancy for breaker panels. The panel is over 30 years old now. As panels age, the safety features within their breakers can begin to fail to function in the event of an electrical fault. Separate from this, should any breakers fail, or need to be replaced, it can be difficult to find replacements as they do not manufacture these parts anymore. I noted that the panel brand, while the breakers are assorted, is a “Challenger”. The Product the Sellers’ have is not one that was inherently recalled, but the company itself has an extensive history of recalls related to breaker failures. I noted several of the Challenger breakers are forming a rather loose connection which can ultimately lead to power failures, or potential overheating. I informed Mr. Sellers that while I didn’t have any immediate concerns, this is something that should begin to take precedence as a project to prevent potential failures down the road. I also encouraged the Sellers’ to run dehumidifiers in the panel spaces as they seem to be falling victim to ambient moisture with time. I have provided an estimate to replace the main breaker panel for all of the above listed reasons, I provided one separate option to run a gas bonding wire to the homes gas piping in order to meet code compliance and safety standards. I understand that you have just moved in, and more than likely were not expecting some of these options, but we want you to know that we are here to guide and help make your new home safe, comfortable, and efficient. Once we got a good understanding of the issue, we then started our thorough evaluation at the electrical panel and then worked their way to the kitchen switches. One year worry free parts and labor warranty will be honored for the new switch that we installed today.

However, when we first arrived at this property, we noticed that the main PPL triplex wire was no longer attached to the home and was starting to pull on the new service wires that LPH installed earlier this year. We contacted PPL to inform them of our findings and got them to schedule some of their technicians to arrive and correct this issue. 

Invoice for today’s visit will be emailed to the homeowner for the record. We thank you for allowing us into your home to service your electrical concern and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

Technician performed a thorough plumbing system inspection on all accessible plumbing fixtures throughout the home to evaluate overall operation, drainage, water flow, and visible plumbing conditions. During the inspection, technician identified a few concerns within the plumbing system and discussed recommended solutions with the homeowner to address the issues found. Technician reviewed available repair and improvement options to help maintain proper system performance and prevent future plumbing problems.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 12 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be 2.0 ppm. A hardness level of 12 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, showerheads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

The homeowner would like to add a hot water supply line for the heated toilet seat in the main-floor hallway bathroom. To complete the installation, the technician will need to shut off the main water supply to the home to make the necessary plumbing connections. Once the work is completed, the water supply will be restored, and the new connection will be checked for proper operation and leaks.

While installing the toilet water line, the technician also completed the previously sold work to finish connecting the front yard exterior hose faucet. The additional work was completed during the same service visit.

Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater to allow for efficient integration into the home’s main water distribution system. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the existing main drain located behind the water heater at the proposed installation area. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. The home’s electrical panel is located approximately 5 feet away, and an outlet will need to be installed and provided at the equipment location prior to or as part of the installation. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 16 grains per gallon (GPG) and the chlorine level to be 1.0 ppm. A hardness level of 16 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, showerheads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

To improve water quality and help protect the home’s plumbing system, technician recommends installing a City Soft water treatment system. The system is designed to soften the water by removing the hardness minerals that cause scale buildup while also reducing chlorine levels throughout the home. Benefits of the system include improved soap and detergent performance, reduced spotting and scaling, softer-feeling water, and increased protection and efficiency of plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances.

The proposed installation location for the City Soft system is near the existing water heater. The water inlet from the water meter to the water softener would have to be routed about the bathroom area in order to supply treated water to home. Water meter is approximately 20’ away from proposed area. The softener’s backwash drain lines will be routed and connected to the washer drain approximately 5’ away. The system also requires a dedicated electrical outlet for operation and regeneration cycles. The home’s electrical panel is located approximately 75 feet away, and an outlet will need to be installed and provided at the equipment location prior to or as part of the installation. Homeowner is going to consult with LPH electrician once they are ready. Once installed, the system will provide conditioned water to the entire home and help minimize the long-term effects of hard water and chlorine exposure on the plumbing system.

Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs. We strive to provide professional, high-quality service on every visit, and your feedback helps us continue improving.

We would greatly appreciate hearing about your experience with the technician who served you today. Your feedback regarding the quality of work performed, communication, professionalism, and overall service is extremely valuable to us.

Thank you again for choosing LPH. We truly appreciate your business and the opportunity to serve you!

Homeowner reported that the water stopped flowing from the well during an evening shower. Technician checked the voltage at the disconnect and pressure switch, measuring 245 volts, and verified voltage across the pressure switch. Technician removed the well cover and discovered that the well pipe had separated from the pitless adapter, leaving the well pump suspended by the electrical wiring. Technician was able to manually retrieve the well pump and remove the pitless adapter, where a broken plastic barbed adapter was discovered.

Technician replaced the broken plastic barbed adapter with a stainless-steel barbed adapter for improved durability and secured the well wiring more securely to the well pipe. Technician checked continuity and measured the well depth at 54 feet, with the well pump positioned at 41 feet. After completing the repairs, Technician reinstalled the well pump into the well casing and restored power to the system. The pump’s amperage draw was measured at 5.7 amps.

The well pump is approximately 16 years old and is currently operating properly based on the technician’s checks. The issue was caused by the failed plastic barbed adapter, which allowed the well pipe to separate from the pitless adapter. The adapter was replaced, and the well system was returned to operation.

Technician also provided a solution for, 

During the well pump diagnostic, Technician noticed that the existing pressure tank and associated fittings are galvanized and appear to be original to the home. Due to the age of these components, Technician recommends proactively updating the pressure tank and related accessories to help maintain the reliability and proper operation of the well water system. The existing galvanized fittings should be removed and replaced with modern fittings, as galvanized piping and fittings can corrode internally over time, potentially restricting water flow and contributing to leaks or other plumbing issues. Updating the pressure tank and its associated components would also provide an opportunity to inspect the connections and related equipment for signs of wear, corrosion, or deterioration. Replacing these aging components can help reduce the risk of unexpected failures, improve system reliability, and provide greater peace of mind regarding the home’s well water system.

Technician performed water quality testing and found the home’s water hardness to be 24 grains per gallon (GPG) and the  level to be 8.0 ppm. A hardness level of 16 GPG is considered hard water and can lead to calcium and magnesium scale buildup inside water heaters, plumbing fixtures, faucets, shower heads, and water-using appliances. Over time, this mineral buildup can reduce appliance efficiency, shorten equipment life expectancy, cause spotting on dishes and glassware, and leave soap residue on fixtures and surfaces. The presence of chlorine, while common in municipal water supplies, can contribute to dry skin and hair and may deteriorate rubber seals and gaskets within the plumbing system over time.

e.346177547:
Instead of having a pressure switch were the psi goes from 30 to 50. This unit gives constant pressure. And it protects the pump from dry firing. A sub drive package for a well system usually refers to a submersible pump drive package or a variable frequency drive (VFD) package used to control a well pump. In water-well and industrial well applications, it allows the pump to operate more efficiently by controlling the speed of its electric motor. 
1. Consistent water pressure
Reduces the pressure swings commonly experienced with traditional pressure-switch systems. Showers, faucets, and irrigation equipment can operate more consistently.
2. Better pump and motor protection
Depending on the model, built-in protections can detect overloads, low motor load associated with dry running, and certain electrical faults. This can help prevent costly damage.
3. Softer starts and stops
The drive gradually ramps motor speed up and down, reducing abrupt starting stresses and potentially reducing pressure surges and mechanical wear.
4. Potential energy savings
When water demand is low, the pump may run at a lower speed and use less power. Actual savings depend on pump sizing, operating conditions, and how much demand varies.
5. Smaller pressure tank
Many constant-pressure installations can use a smaller tank than a conventional on/off system, saving space and potentially reducing installation complexity.
6. Better control of well production
The pump can be adjusted to match water demand and, when properly configured, help limit pumping to the well's sustainable yield. This is particularly valuable for low-yield wells.

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

Thank you for trusting LPH with your plumbing needs. We strive to provide professional, high-quality service on every visit, and your feedback helps us continue improving.

We would greatly appreciate hearing about your experience with the technician who served you today. Your feedback regarding the quality of work performed, communication, professionalism, and overall service is extremely valuable to us.

The homeowner reported experiencing low water pressure from the well system for approximately two months. Technician verified that the pressure switch was receiving the proper voltage of 248 VAC. Technician then shut off the breaker to the well pump and drained the pressure tank, confirming that the tank pressure was at 0 PSI. Technician attempted to recharge the pressure tank with air but found that the internal bladder would not hold air, indicating that the pressure tank has failed and requires replacement.
During the inspection, Technician also observed that the existing brass tank tee assembly was badly corroded. LPH arrived at the residence to evaluate the existing electrical system and discuss recommended improvements to enhance electrical safety, reliability, and protection throughout the home.

Basement Trough and Disconnect Replacement:

Upon inspection, LPH identified extensive rust and corrosion within the existing basement electrical trough, indicating a history of water intrusion and moisture exposure. The moisture has affected the wiring connections, leaving a film of oxidation and corrosion on the connection points and lugs. Corroded connections can increase electrical resistance, generate excessive heat, and compromise the reliability of the electrical system.

Additionally, the disconnect supplying the upstairs bedroom electrical panel has exceeded its recommended service life and shows considerable rust and corrosion throughout the enclosure. The internal lugs have also developed oxidation and corrosion, further compromising the integrity of the electrical connections. This disconnect contains a discontinued Zinsco breaker, a product line widely associated with serious safety concerns, including breakers that may fail to trip during an overload or short circuit, overheating, and connections that can deteriorate over time. These concerns can increase the risk of electrical fires and may also create complications during insurance reviews or real estate transactions.

LPH recommends replacing the existing trough and disconnect arrangement with a new electrical trough mounted securely to a backer board. The existing wiring will be reconnected using heavy-duty Polaris insulated connectors, providing secure, reliable connections. A new 100-amp disconnect will also be installed on the backer board to supply the upstairs electrical panel. This replacement will eliminate the deteriorated equipment and outdated disconnect, improve the integrity of the electrical connections, and provide a safer, more dependable electrical distribution setup.

Whole-Home Surge Protection:

During the inspection, LPH also identified deterioration affecting the electronic driver components of the arc-fault circuit interrupter (AFCI) breaker in the upstairs electrical panel. This is the only AFCI breaker currently installed in the home. Electronic components can experience wear and deterioration over time from transient voltage spikes that occur throughout a home’s electrical system. These voltage fluctuations can be generated when motor-driven equipment, such as air conditioners, refrigerators, and other appliances, cycles on and off. Utility-related disturbances and lightning can also introduce damaging voltage surges.

LPH recommends installing a premium whole-home surge protector at the electrical service equipment. This device helps limit damaging transient overvoltages before they reach connected circuits and sensitive electronic equipment. By reducing exposure to these voltage spikes, whole-home surge protection can help protect appliance control boards, televisions, computers, and other valuable electronics, potentially extending their service life and reducing the likelihood of costly premature failures. While no surge protector can eliminate every electrical threat, this upgrade provides an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical system and connected equipment.

Exterior Receptacle Safety Improvements:

During the evaluation, LPH discovered that the exterior receptacles lack GFCI protection and that two of the existing receptacles have improper covers. The receptacles currently installed are intended for indoor use and have deteriorated significantly from prolonged exposure to outdoor conditions. Moisture intrusion and corrosion can compromise receptacle connections, increase the likelihood of electrical failures, and create potential shock hazards.

LPH recommends replacing the affected exterior receptacles with weather-resistant devices designed for outdoor applications. The proposed improvements include one weather-resistant receptacle, three weather-resistant GFCI receptacles, and two extra-duty in-use bubble covers. GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of serious electrical shock by quickly interrupting power when a ground fault is detected. The weather-resistant receptacles and properly rated covers will provide improved protection against rain, moisture, and environmental exposure. The in-use bubble covers are designed to help protect receptacles while cords are plugged in, providing an additional layer of protection against water intrusion.

These improvements will address the deteriorated exterior devices, bring the receptacle installations closer to current safety expectations, and provide more dependable outdoor electrical service.

LPH recommends completing these improvements to address the existing corrosion, eliminate the outdated Zinsco disconnect, improve electrical connection reliability, and add protection against electrical shock and damaging voltage surges. Together, these upgrades will help improve the overall safety, reliability, and long-term performance of the home’s electrical system.

A water softener removes or reduces the minerals that cause hard water, mainly calcium and magnesium. If your home has hard water, a water softener can make a noticeable difference in cleaning, bathing, and maintaining appliances.
The 7 main benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale buildup
Reduces white, chalky deposits on faucets, showerheads, sinks, glass shower doors, and inside plumbing and water-heating equipment.
2. Softer-feeling skin and hair
Many people find their skin feels less dry and their hair feels smoother because soap rinses away more easily. It won't cure skin conditions, however.
3. Softer, cleaner laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, detergent works more effectively, and mineral deposits on fabrics can be reduced.
4. Cleaner dishes and glassware
Helps prevent cloudy spots and mineral film on glasses, silverware, and dishes.
5. Helps protect appliances
Reduces scale inside water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other water-using equipment. This can help maintain efficiency and reduce maintenance.
6. Less soap and detergent needed
Soft water allows soap to lather more easily, so you may use less shampoo, body wash, laundry detergent, and household cleaning products.
7. Easier household cleaning
Less time spent scrubbing mineral deposits off shower doors, faucets, sinks, and bathroom fixtures.

e.347424172:
The Moen Flo Smart Water Monitor & Shutoff is a smart-home device designed to help protect your house from water leaks and flooding. It installs on your main water line and monitors your home's water use 24/7. Unlike a water softener, it doesn't soften water or remove minerals — its main purpose is to prevent water damage.
The 6 biggest benefits of Moen Flo
1. Automatically shuts off water during a potential leak
If it detects a serious leak or unusual water usage, Flo can close your home's main water valve to help prevent flooding. This is especially valuable if a washing machine hose, toilet supply line, or pipe fails while you're away. 
2. Detects small hidden leaks
Its daily MicroLeak tests can identify leaks as small as approximately one drop per minute, potentially catching a slow leak behind a wall or under a floor before it causes extensive damage. 
3. Protects your home when you're on vacation
You can receive alerts remotely and shut off the water through the app. Automatic shutoff adds another layer of protection when nobody is home to notice a burst pipe or leaking appliance. 
4. Helps reduce water waste
Flo tracks water flow, pressure, and usage patterns. You may discover running toilets, dripping fixtures, or other problems that increase your water bill. 
5. Monitors water pressure and temperature
It can flag unusual pressure or flow conditions and send freezing-condition warnings, helping you spot potential plumbing problems early. 
6. May help reduce expensive water-damage repairs
Catching a leak early can help protect hardwood floors, drywall, ceilings, cabinets, and finished basements. Some insurers may also offer discounts for qualifying leak-prevention systems.

e.346733744:
Summary: Replacement of Saniflo Toilet Pump

The existing Saniflo Saniplus macerator pump was identified as not pumping properly, with the motor humming or running without effectively discharging wastewater. The planned work is to replace the complete macerator unit. The replacement process includes shutting off the water supply and disconnecting the electrical power, draining the unit as safely as possible, disconnecting the toilet inlet and discharge pipework, and removing the existing macerator. The new unit will be installed using the correct seals and compatible plumbing connections, ensuring that all pipework and discharge connections are properly secured. Once installation is complete, the water supply and electrical power will be restored, and the system will be tested to verify proper operation, effective waste discharge, and leak-free connections. All work will be carried out in accordance with the manufacturer’s installation instructions and applicable plumbing and electrical safety requirements.

Depending on the pump, technician may have to cut open some drywall to access piping.

A water softener removes or reduces hardness minerals—mainly calcium and magnesium—from your household water. It can make a noticeable difference in cleaning, bathing, plumbing, and appliance maintenance, especially if you have hard water.
7 main benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale buildup
Reduces white, chalky deposits on showerheads, faucets, sinks, and glass. It also helps prevent scale buildup inside pipes and water heaters.
2. Softer-feeling skin and hair
Soap rinses away more easily, and some people notice less residue, dryness, or stiffness in their hair. Results vary depending on your skin and hair type.
3. Softer, cleaner laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, and mineral deposits on fabrics can be reduced.
4. Less soap and detergent
Soft water allows soap to lather more readily, so you may need less laundry detergent, dish soap, and some cleaning products.
5. Better appliance efficiency
Helps reduce scale in water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and other water-using appliances. This can help maintain efficiency and reduce maintenance.
6. Easier household cleaning
Less mineral spotting on glassware, shower doors, and fixtures means less scrubbing and fewer specialized descaling products.
7. Helps protect plumbing
Reducing mineral scale can help keep pipes, valves, and fixtures working properly, particularly in homes with very hard water.

i.346729269: LPH arrived at the Jacunski family home to conduct their annual electrical system check. Upon performing an annual electrical system and safety check I found no major discrepancies. I noted a couple of double tapped breakers in the main breaker panel which I provided an estimate to replace. Double tapped breakers mean there is a single breaker supplying two or more separate circuits. These breakers are only designed to support one circuit. When they have two or more, it can be difficult for the single wire lug to make a secure connection to both lines, over time these lugs can work themselves loose and lead to potential overheating. This can cause damage to both the circuit, the breaker, and the panels bus bar. I provided a solution to install tandem breakers in order to remove the double tapped set up. I provided an additional solution to replace a faulty timer inside of a landscape lighting transformer located on the back of the home. It seems as though the gearing within the timer is not making proper contact, and in turn it isn’t actuating the on and off switch for the lights. I was able to manually turn the gears and restore power to the lights to verify proper function through the rest of the system. Otherwise, the home appears to be in good electrical condition. If you have any questions, or if you would like to move forward with these options, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you!

e.347607310:
A water softener can make a noticeable difference in your home, especially if you have hard water, which contains high levels of calcium and magnesium. It replaces or removes these minerals to reduce the problems they cause.
7 key benefits of a water softener
1. Less limescale and mineral buildup
Helps prevent white, chalky deposits on faucets, showerheads, glass shower doors, sinks, and inside pipes.
2. Softer skin and smoother-feeling hair
Reduces mineral residue that can leave skin feeling dry or hair feeling rough. It may help soap rinse away more easily, although it won't treat underlying skin or scalp conditions.
3. Softer laundry
Clothes and towels may feel less stiff, colors can stay brighter, and less detergent is generally needed.
4. Cleaner dishes and glassware
Can reduce cloudy spots and mineral film on glasses, silverware, and dishes.
5. Helps protect plumbing and appliances
Reduces scale accumulation in water heaters, dishwashers, washing machines, and pipes, potentially improving efficiency and extending equipment life.
6. Less soap and detergent
Soft water allows soap to lather more readily, so you may use less laundry detergent, dish soap, shampoo, and body wash.
7. Easier household cleaning
Less time scrubbing mineral deposits from showers, tubs, sinks, and fixtures.

The water softener also gets rid of the chlorine in the water. Chlorine is a chemical and is unsafe to consume. It gets consumed whenever you shower, wash your hands, etc. 


This option does not include having electrical ran to the unit. If there is no outlet for the unit to plug-in further charges may apply. Technician may also have to open up some drywall.

The Moen Flo Smart Water Monitor and Shutoff is a smart device installed on your home's main water line. Its biggest benefit is that it can detect unusual water use, alert you to potential leaks, and automatically shut off your home's water to help prevent expensive flooding.  
1. Helps prevent catastrophic water damage
If a pipe bursts, a toilet supply line fails, or an appliance hose leaks, Flo can detect abnormal water flow and automatically shut off the main water supply. This may prevent thousands of dollars in damage.
2. Detects small hidden leaks
Its daily MicroLeak tests can identify leaks as small as approximately one drop per minute, helping uncover problems in plumbing that you might not otherwise notice.
3. Protects your home while you're away
Receive alerts on your phone when unusual water use or potential leaks are detected. This is especially valuable on vacation, at a second home, or when you're away at work.
4. Monitors water consumption
Track water usage, flow rate, and pressure. This can help you spot running toilets, unexpected water consumption, or other potential plumbing problems.
5. Lets you shut off water remotely
You can turn off your home's water from the app if you suspect a problem or want to shut it off while away, without needing to be physically at the valve.
6. May reduce insurance costs
Some insurers offer discounts for approved automatic water shutoff devices. Eligibility and savings depend on your insurance company, so check before purchasing.

This option does not include having electrical ran to the unit. If there is no where to plug into further charges may apply. Technician may also have to open up drywall.

Today, I completed the annual electrical system inspection. Upon evaluation, I found the main electrical panel to be in excellent condition, with no signs of rust or corrosion. All electrical connections were verified to be tight, no signs of overheating were observed, and voltage readings were confirmed to be within acceptable ranges.

However, I did note that the main panel is not equipped with a whole-home surge protection device. This device is important for protecting the home’s electrical equipment and appliances from voltage surges.

I also observed that the exterior service entrance wiring is in very poor condition. This is common with wiring that has been exposed to direct sunlight for many years, as prolonged UV exposure can cause the outer insulation to deteriorate and crack. Once the insulation is compromised, moisture can enter and travel into the electrical panel, potentially causing rust and corrosion to the connections and resulting in more extensive and costly repairs.

I discussed these findings with the customer and explained that, given the condition of the existing meter base and service components, replacing only the wiring between the panel and the meter would still require an inspection and coordination with the utility company to disconnect and restore power. Therefore, I recommended replacing the entire service to address the existing issues and avoid additional labor and potential future repairs.

The recommended service replacement would include new service entrance wiring, PVC conduit to provide additional protection and extend the life of the wiring, a new meter base, and a slip riser.

The invoice and estimate were emailed to the customer for review.

This will help maintain the water seals in the P-traps and reduce the likelihood of sewer gas odors.

i.346874066:
We were called out to evaluate Robert issue with his bathroom GFI on the first floor, constantly tripping and not being able to be reset. Robert also showed us, some other locations that were affected. We started our thorough evaluation at the main electrical panel to identify if this was a power supply issue or if it was an issue with the circuit that this GFI was protecting. We were able to identify that the power supply for the GFI was in really good shape and not the issue. We were able to identify one of the exterior outlets are a part of this circuit. This exterior plug contained two cords actively used at this receptacle. We unplugged both of these cords, reset the GFI, and identified that the system was functioning correctly. While the system was still on, we then re-plugged in the cords back into the exterior outlet and noticed that this GFI tripped again with the gazebo ceiling fan cord. Upon further inspection of this cord, we noticed that the ceiling fan cord was plugged into another extension cord, which had water stuck in between the plug joint. Once we unplugged this plug joint, the GFI was able to reset and functioning. We informed and showed Robert the main culprit of his issue and provided an option to install receptacle underneath the gazebo roof where the ceiling fan cord can plug into without having this issue. We also identified the exterior receptacle has seen some signs of weather and should be replaced as preventative maintenance.

Prior to leaving, Robert had another question with his bathroom lighting that would be delayed when turning on. We did a thorough evaluation and some research, coming to the conclusion that the quality of the bulbs should be where we start and then build on from there. We recommend high-quality Phillips LED lightbulbs to replace the existing mid grade supply house bulbs, that were existing. 

Robert opted to have the solutions provided for the gazebo emailed for his record and to review. We collected the dispatch fee for today’s troubleshooting and diagnostics. We thank you for trusting LPH and we look forward to servicing in the future.

i.346932418:
Electrical System Check Evaluation

LPH completed an electrical system check to evaluate the condition of the home’s electrical components, identify existing concerns, and provide recommendations for improving the safety, reliability, and overall condition of the electrical system.

During the evaluation, several areas of concern were identified, including the age and condition of the existing electrical service equipment, deficiencies in the home’s grounding and bonding system, and multiple interior electrical devices that have deteriorated due to overheating and electrical arcing.

1. Main Electrical Service and Panel

The existing electrical service is rated at 100 amps and is estimated to be up to 45 years old. The main electrical panel is a discontinued model, and the exterior meter base exhibits extensive rust and corrosion affecting both the exterior and interior of the equipment. The existing exterior service cables are also aged and dry-rotted. This type of cable is known to allow moisture intrusion through deterioration of its outer jacket, potentially compromising the conductors inside.

Given the age and condition of these components, LPH recommends a complete upgrade to a new 200-amp electrical service. This would replace the existing service equipment and wiring with new components, including a meter base, exterior emergency disconnect, service cables, PVC conduit, and service head. The upgrade would also include a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel with all new breakers and premium whole-home surge protection.

The existing equipment has reached a stage in its service life where continued reliance on these components raises concerns regarding long-term reliability, moisture intrusion, and potential electrical connection failures. Replacing the service would address these concerns while providing additional electrical capacity for the home’s future needs.

2. Grounding and Bonding System

The existing grounding arrangement is improper and currently relies on a connection to a water pipe above the electrical panel, with a separate small jumper to the meter. LPH recommends correcting the grounding and bonding system to meet applicable electrical code requirements.

A separate estimate has been provided for these grounding improvements, including installing two new ground rods, establishing a continuous grounding connection to the home’s incoming water service piping, and properly bonding the gas piping system.

Please note that the complete grounding and bonding improvements are already included as part of the proposed 200-amp electrical service upgrade. If the homeowners elect to proceed with the complete service replacement, the separate grounding estimate would not need to be completed as an additional project.

3. Deteriorated Receptacles and Basement Light Switch

During the evaluation, three receptacles were identified as deteriorated and damaged, with signs of loosening and overheating associated with excessive electrical loads. These conditions can compromise the electrical connections and increase the potential for continued overheating, electrical arcing, and further device damage.

Additionally, the switch controlling the basement lighting has deteriorated and produces electrical arcing when switched on and off.

LPH recommends replacing all three affected receptacles and the deteriorated basement light switch. Accessible wiring and connections should also be inspected during replacement for any additional signs of heat damage or deterioration that may require repair.

Addressing these issues will help restore reliable operation and reduce the risks associated with continued use of damaged electrical devices.

4. Proposed 60-Amp Electrical Feed to the Garage for a Tesla Supercharger

The current tenant also expressed interest in installing a new electrical feed to the garage to accommodate a Tesla Supercharger and indicated that he may be interested in covering the cost of the project.

At the tenant’s request and based on the proposed installation, LPH prepared a separate estimate for a new 60-amp electrical feed extending from the home’s main panel to the detached garage. The proposed installation includes the necessary exterior conduit, service head and point of attachment, overhead triplex cable, garage riser, interior feeder wiring, a new 60-amp disconnect, and wiring extending to the designated charger location.

This project is contingent on completing the proposed 200-amp electrical service upgrade. The existing 100-amp service would need to be upgraded before proceeding with the proposed installation, subject to verification of the available service capacity and the final electrical requirements of the charging equipment.

5. Estimates and Property Owner Authorization

The proposed 200-amp service upgrade and the new electrical feed to the garage were discussed after the current tenant expressed interest in having this work completed and potentially paying for the projects himself with permission from the property owners.

LPH prepared these estimates to provide the property owners with clear pricing and an understanding of the proposed work. The estimates are being provided for the homeowners’ review and consideration, and the decision to proceed with any of the proposed improvements, regardless of whether the tenant offers to cover the costs, is entirely at the property owners’ discretion.

Although the tenant initiated the discussion regarding the service upgrade and garage feed, LPH independently recommends the complete 200-amp service upgrade due to the age, deterioration, and overall condition of the existing electrical service components. This recommendation is based on the findings of the electrical evaluation, not solely on the proposed Tesla charging installation.

The separate grounding estimate is available for consideration if the homeowners choose not to proceed with the complete service upgrade. However, the grounding improvements are already included in the full 200-amp service replacement estimate.

Conclusion

LPH has provided separate estimates outlining the recommended repairs and potential upgrades identified during the electrical system check. These options include replacing the deteriorated receptacles and basement light switch, correcting the grounding and bonding system, upgrading the existing 100-amp service to 200 amps, and installing a new 60-amp electrical feed to the garage for the proposed Tesla Supercharger.

The service upgrade is the primary recommendation due to the age and deteriorated condition of the existing service equipment and wiring. The remaining options have been presented to give the property owners a clear understanding of the identified concerns, available improvements, and associated costs.

LPH will email all estimates and the completed electrical evaluation to the property owners for their review and consideration.
